The latest research turns this process into an agentic pipeline comprising five stages -      Vulnerability discovery, where agents identify high-value audit targets (i.e., parts of the codebase that are security-relevant and reachable by low-privileged users) and look for candidate findings    Dynamic validation, where agents attempt to reproduce each candidate ...
content:
OpenAI on Wednesday detailed a pipeline that employed an upcoming cyber-focused artificial intelligence (AI) model to validate and patch 948 local privilege escalation vulnerabilities in Linux for $1.2 million in API costs.

"Our prototype identified and analyzed 2,308 candidate Linux kernel findings, dynamically reproduced 1,724 vulnerabilities, and produced 948 local privilege escalation (LPE) exploits that could allow an unprivileged local user to gain root access," the AI company said.

The findings build upon 24 LPE exploits that OpenAI revealed were discovered by its GPT‑5.5‑Cyber model back in June 2026. The latest research turns this process into an agentic pipeline comprising five stages -

  • Vulnerability discovery, where agents identify high-value audit targets (i.e., parts of the codebase that are security-relevant and reachable by low-privileged users) and look for candidate findings
  • Dynamic validation, where agents attempt to reproduce each candidate in a sandboxed environment and preserve runtime evidence
  • Exploitability assessment, where agents test whether validated vulnerabilities could be abused to facilitate information disclosure or LPE and devise a proof-of-concept (PoC) exploit
  • Patch generation, where agents generate patches for the identified vulnerability
  • Human review, where security researchers review the exploit, patch, and proposed severity before it's reported to the maintainers

"In a run in mid-October 2026, our pipeline using an upcoming cyber model dynamically reproduced 1,724 vulnerabilities [within 30 hours] and generated PoCs for 291 information leak vulnerabilities and 948 working local privilege escalation (LPE) exploits for a commonly used Linux distribution," OpenAI said.

"The total run cost $1,213,430 in API credits, or $1,279 per LPE exploit. To the best of our knowledge, the agents in this pipeline discovered and used at least 10 novel Linux exploitation techniques."

At a high level, these include -

  • Two new persistent elastic objects to spray objects inside the target kernel cache
  • Two new page grooming techniques to improve exploit reliability
  • Five new data-only techniques to obtain privilege escalation directly or via an arbitrary write
  • One technique that involves arbitrary type confusion

The development is once again an indication of how frontier AI is redrawing the contours of cybersecurity, accelerating vulnerability discovery and exploitation, and at the same time helping defenders reliably address defects, albeit through additional instructions and iterations, before attackers can use them, and make it "cost prohibitive" for bad actors to exploit software.

In a report published last month, VulnCheck categorized AI-assisted vulnerability discovery as a "growing risk category" that turbocharges novice hackers, who now require little to no technical expertise to detect software vulnerabilities.

The access to AI models is not just limited to defenders, but also bad actors who can leverage the same capabilities to discover and weaponize new zero-days and expand the pool of viable targets with minimal effort.

According to insights from Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG), the number of vulnerabilities disclosed per month has more than doubled, rising from 5,045 in January 2026 to 10,740 in August 2026. The number of vulnerabilities classified as high-risk has surged from 131 disclosures in January 2026 to 350 in August 2026, a 167% growth.

"The widespread availability of AI-powered cyber tools has almost certainly led to a significant increase in the discovery of zero-day vulnerabilities," the U.K. National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) said in an assessment published Tuesday.

"Defensive AI-cyber tools have reduced the window of a vulnerability moving from zero-day to an N-day vulnerability, and have made patching a quicker process. However, without correct and widespread configuring of this technology, many systems are still vulnerable to attackers using AI-cyber tools to identify and exploit system weaknesses."

The NCSC also pointed out that organizations will have to evolve their internal patching and testing processes to meet this new pace of vulnerability discovery.

"Attackers have subsequently displayed less caution over losing an access to achieve an objective, as the cost to replace is minimal," it added. "Cyber capabilities are now used for a broader range of activity due to the lower risk involved, making it easier for adversaries to access information and use it operationally."

OpenAI said the rate of vulnerability discovery by frontier models needs to be matched by automated patch generation to secure software and to limit the exploitation window.

"With human expert-guided iteration, we believe AI-generated patches can be functionally correct, aligned with existing coding styles, and robust to attack variants," OpenAI said. "For the near and medium term, having access to a low-privileged account on an operating system that isn't up-to-date on its latest available patches should be considered functionally equivalent to root access for a well-resourced threat actor."

title: GOG is hosting its first gaming showcase event — here's where and when you can watch it
author: Alexander Cope
summary: GOG, a beloved digital storefront for releasing DRM-free PC games and long-awaited PC ports of classic games, has announced its very first "GOG Showcase" event, where it will reveal new games, feature...
content:
GOG is one of the world's most popular digital storefronts for PC games. It's beloved by players for releasing PC games without DRM restrictions and releasing long-awaited ports of classic games like Breath of Fire 4 and Dino Crisis, fully updated to run on modern PCs.

GOG has reached its 18th anniversary this year. To celebrate, it will be hosting its first-ever gaming showcase event called the "GOG Showcase" on November 5, 2026, to reveal new games, new features, and more surprises as it enters a new chapter.

The GOG Showcase will be broadcast on GOG's YouTube channel at 7:00 PM CET / 1:00 PM ET / 10:00 AM PT / 6:00 PM GMT.

Windows Central's take

GOG Showcase | New games. New features. New chapter! - YouTube
Watch On

GOG has gained a surge in popularity this year as it's become a champion for preserving not only classic games but also consumers' rights and true digital ownership of games (which is becoming rarer in the wake of PlayStation killing physical discs or Microsoft blocking players' entire Xbox game libraries).

Granted, it isn't entirely perfect, as over a thousand games on GOG are missing DLC, updates, and other features compared to their Steam or Epic Games Store counterparts.

You may like
  • PC Gaming Show Tokyo Direct: Start times, platforms, and more
  • Watch times and platforms for the Future Games Show at Gamescom 2026
  • 1,140 GOG games lack content or have other issues compared to competing storefronts

However, when it comes to providing games players can keep forever with their own dedicated launchers and with no DRM to hinder their performance (with a 30-day return as a bonus), GOG has its competition beat in that regard.

So I'm looking forward to seeing what retro games from the past GOG plans to bring back next on PC when the GOG Showcase begins tomorrow (fingers crossed they bring back the PS1 JRPG classic, Legend of Dragoon).

title: Windows 11 using most of your RAM? Microsoft says that’s a good thing, as...
author: Abhijith M B
summary: After a restart with no apps installed, Windows 11 used 2.4GB on a 4GB VM and 3.7GB on a 16GB VM. Microsoft’s documentation explains why Windows keeps more pages in RAM when memory is abundant, what A...
content:
Task Manager showing 70% or even 90% of your RAM in use doesn’t mean your Windows 11 PC is running out of memory, according to Windows boss Pavan Davuluri. Windows keeps apps and data you might need in spare RAM, and hands it back when another app asks.

Funnily enough, Davuluri explains it with a desk and a drawer, just like I did in my page file explainer two weeks ago. To make things interesting, I also restarted a Windows 11 virtual machine with 4GB, 8GB, and 16GB of RAM, and the more memory I gave to Windows, the more it used.

Why a nearly full Task Manager doesn’t mean Windows 11 is short on RAM

In his November 3 blog post on 8GB PCs, Davuluri compares RAM to your desk and your SSD to a drawer. Anything moved to the drawer takes longer to fetch, which is why an app you left open can take a second to come back. “A full desk is a good thing,” he wrote, and “The real test is whether your PC stays responsive, not how much memory remains unused.”

I’ve seen people on socials say unused RAM is wasted RAM, and Microsoft’s Memory Footprint documentation tells us the origins of this idea. It splits RAM into In use, which covers the working sets of Windows and your apps plus non-paged memory and modified pages, and Available, which is free memory plus standby memory, or “cached data and files that are in memory but not in active use.”

Standby memory “becomes available as an application needs it,” so Task Manager’s Available number already includes cache Windows can give away. Cached is complicated, as Microsoft’s AskPerf team explains that it adds up the system working set, the standby list, and modified pages, overlapping both In use and Available. On my 8GB VM, 2.9GB in use and 5.1GB available make up the full 8GB, and the 2.1GB cached is spread across both.

Windows also compresses less-active data, and Davuluri says new tuning on 8GB PCs keeps up to 2GB more of your active data in RAM, so fewer apps reload.

I checked Windows 11 on 4GB, 8GB and 16GB VMs, and RAM usage grew with more RAM

Windows Latest set up a VMware virtual machines on Windows 11 26H2 Build 26340.9843, and doubled the RAM two times, starting with 4GB. I restarted after each RAM increase and opened Task Manager > Performance > Memory.

VM RAM In use Available Cached Committed
4GB 2.4GB (60%) 1.6GB 1.3GB 2.2GB / 5.6GB
8GB 2.9GB (36%) 5.1GB 2.1GB 2.4GB / 9.6GB
16GB 3.7GB (23%) 12.3GB 1.9GB 3.3GB / 18.4GB

The 16GB VM used 1.3GB more than the 4GB one. Compressed memory was strangely 0MB on all three, so none was under pressure after boot, probably because the VM is devoid of any memory-sucking apps and is mostly clean.

Interestingly, committed memory barely moved between the 4GB and 8GB VMs (2.2GB vs 2.4GB), while In use grew by 0.5GB. Microsoft’s Raymond Chen describes commit as “the promise to produce memory upon access,” which suggests the 8GB VM kept more pages in RAM instead of allocating more memory.

Microsoft’s SetProcessWorkingSetSizeEx documentation says, “If memory is abundant, the system might allow an application to exceed its maximum working set limit.” My educated guess is that with 12.3GB available, Windows had little reason to trim anything on the 16GB VM.

In addition to that, Windows loads different things depending on your RAM. Davuluri’s post says Widgets now loads only when you open it on PCs with 8GB or less, cutting roughly 200MB of committed memory, and my 16GB VM doesn’t qualify, which could explain part of its jump in committed memory from 2.4GB to 3.3GB.

However, the theory that Windows caches more apps when it has more RAM didn’t quite hold up as well as I presumed, as Cached was 1.9GB on the 16GB VM, lower than 2.1GB on the 8GB VM. Of course, these are snapshots after a restart on an Insider build, and only Sysinternals RAMMap can show which pages belong to what.

Microsoft may be right about the desk thing, but the truth is that some of what filled it wasn’t useful. After I updated my dad’s 8GB laptop to 26H2, RAM usage after a restart fell from 5GB to 3.3GB, and my 16GB laptop used up to 2GB less. 26H2 is just an enablement package that switched on months of work, so Windows 11 was eating more RAM than it needed long before Microsoft fixed it.

When high RAM usage on Windows 11 becomes a problem

Microsoft’s Working Set page says a soft page fault is resolved without having to read from the drive, like when a page is still cached in RAM. But a hard page fault reads it back from the page file or the original file, and these trips to the drawer are what we perceive as lags or jitter.

In Task Manager, you only need to worry when Available is close to zero, Compressed keeps climbing, and Committed nears its limit, which is your RAM plus the page file (5.6GB on my 4GB VM). Microsoft warns that reaching the commit limit “can cause freezing, crashing, and other malfunctions.”

If that happens, first, panic; second, go find the culprit from Processes, which on my PCs is almost always a browser or a web app like WhatsApp. Remember that most RAM cleaner apps empty standby memory and it won’t help, as Windows has to read that data from your drive again.

Activity Monitor on Mac shows a Memory Pressure graph that takes into consideration the free memory, swap rate, and cached files, while Windows 11’s Task Manager forces us to decode a bunch of numbers.

title: Microsoft confirms direct Wi-Fi for the Xbox Nano controller plus you can use your phone as a TV gamepad.
author: Jennifer Young
summary: Microsoft has launched two Xbox Cloud Gaming previews: direct Wi-Fi "Cloud Connect" for the Nano controller, and a virtual smartphone controller for Smart TVs.
content:
The Xbox Nano's worst-kept secret is finally out in the open, and Xbox Cloud Gaming is more accessible than ever.

We’ve been following the ultra-portable Xbox Nano Controller since its initial reveal, and while its pocket-friendly, SNES-inspired design has been the main talking point, we were pretty bemused by the lack of Wi-Fi capabilities. However, as the controller landed in reviewers hands, it turned out there was indeed Direct to Wifi connection included but Microsoft had kept it a secret for some unknown reason. Today, Xbox officially revealed the news officially. The much-anticipated direct Wi-Fi connection feature, officially dubbed "Cloud Connect", is rolling out in preview.

But the real surprise reveal lies in the rest of the announcement. Xbox have also announced a brand-new feature that lets you use your smartphone as a virtual controller for Xbox Cloud Gaming on supported Smart TVs. This will truly open Cloud Gaming up wide to loads of people who want to try it out.

Here is everything you need to know about the new updates and how to test them out.

The Nano's secret weapon: Cloud Connect

If you caught our preview of the Xbox Nano Controller, you already knew this was coming. Up until now, playing Xbox Cloud Gaming on a TV or web browser meant connecting your controller via Bluetooth. While functional, Bluetooth does introduce an extra layer of input latency before your command even begins its journey to the cloud servers.

Cloud Connect bypasses that entirely. By using a direct Wi-Fi connection from the Xbox Nano Controller straight to Microsoft’s cloud servers, input latency is significantly reduced, making gameplay feel noticeably more responsive. It is the exact same approach that Google Stadia's controller used, and bringing it to the Xbox ecosystem is a massive win for cloud players.

You may like
  • Microsoft reveals a new pocket-sized Xbox Nano Controller
  • XBOX's 'Nano' Controller launches today for $49.99 — An ultra-compact alternative
  • Xbox’s smallest controller is pocket-sized, rechargeable, and only $50

How to try it out:

Currently, the Cloud Connect preview is restricted to players in the US, and it is limited to supported Smart TVs and web browser experiences.

To set it up, you will need to configure the Nano Controller to your home Wi-Fi network. You can do this using the Xbox beta app on Android, or the Xbox Accessories app on PC (note: PC setup requires you to be enrolled in the Xbox Insider program). Once connected to your Wi-Fi, simply launch a supported Xbox Cloud Gaming session and sign in with the same Xbox account used during your setup. The controller will handle the rest.

The best news, your phone is now an Xbox controller?

The Nano getting Wi-Fi Connect wasn't really the biggest news today. If you want to fire up a cloud game on your Smart TV but don't have a physical controller handy, Microsoft has rolled out a solution: your phone.

In a new global preview available on supported Smart TVs where Xbox Cloud Gaming is live, players can now use an iOS or Android smartphone as a virtual gamepad.

The controls load entirely within your phone's web browser, meaning there is no bulky companion app required to get started. Even better, Xbox confirmed that some games will feature custom-tailored touch layouts specifically designed for how they play, rather than just slapping a generic digital gamepad on your screen.

How to try it out:

To access the virtual phone controller, boot up the latest Xbox Cloud Gaming app on your supported Smart TV and navigate to Settings > Account. Toggle on Preview Features. From there, whenever you launch a game without a physical controller connected to the TV, you will be prompted with an option to link your phone for that session.

Both of these features are still in their testing phases, so expect the occasional hiccup and a limited roster of fully supported titles while Microsoft gathers telemetry and player feedback. You can check out the official support page for guidance.

Behold the sheer convenience of using your phone for a quick Vampire Survivors run on the living room TV!

title: Start11 v3 gives Windows 11 a Mac-like makeover, and I love it
author: Sean Endicott
summary: Start11 v3 brings Start menu widgets, Taskbar Islands, and app grouping to Windows 11 in a major update for desktop customization.
content:
The Windows 11 Start menu has received a lot of updates recently, but if you want to fully customize your Start menu, you need to use an app like Start11. A major update to Start11 is now in beta, and it brings a bunch of new features.

Start11 v3 adds support for widgets within the Start menu. There are 20 widgets available at launch, though most are fairly straightforward. Widgets like a clock or calendar may serve better as proof of concept than a core part of the Start menu.

The updated app also adds Taskbar Islands, which are a dock-like experience. They feel a little bit like macOS because they split the taskbar into smaller pieces that do not take up an entire section at the bottom of your screen. But the Taskbar Islands very much match the overall design and feel of Windows 11.

Latest Videos FromWindows Central

Start11 adds support for grouping applications directly in the taskbar by holding Alt and dragging applications together. You can pin those groups as workspaces to launch multiple apps with a single click.

A new button in the taskbar provides quick access to recently closed applications, overflow items, and taskbar tools.

  • 3 Windows 11 tweaks for the September update I recommend

Stardock also added the ability to explore Start menu layouts from the community.

As much as I love apps that customize the look of Windows 11 and add new features, I only keep a few installed on my PC. Start11 is on the short list of apps I install right away, alongside PowerToys.

With Microsoft's recent improvements to the Start menu, an app like Start11 needs to do more to stand out. Start11 v3 does that with taskbar islands, widgets in the Start menu, and other new features.

title: Honeycomb Aeronautical Foxtrot Takeoff Kit: This should be sold separately
author: Ben Wilson
summary: An excellent flight stick gets a useful throttle box upgrade, but existing Honeycomb Foxtrot owners can't buy the missing piece separately.
content:
I've been eagerly waiting for this bundle to launch since I tested Honeycomb's prototype last year, and even more so when the standalone Foxtrot stick won my highest praise. Still, even though it remains my favorite flightstick for Microsoft Flight Simulator, the Foxtrot always felt like it was missing that compact throttle box. Problem solved.

Why you should trust me
Why you should trust me
Ben Wilson
Senior Editor, Flight Sim Enjoyer

I became a fast fan of Microsoft Flight Simulator when it came to XBOX in 2020, and its sequel still holds my attention when paired with a reasonably priced throttle-and-stick setup — of which I've tested my fair share.

Disclaimer

Honeycomb Aeronautical provided a sample but did not see, nor did it have any input on, the contents of my article before publishing.

How much does the Foxtrot Takeoff Kit cost?

You'll find the Foxtrot Takeoff Kit for $179.99 at Honeycomb's own store or through approved third-party US resellers such as Sporty's and Focus Camera. Over in the United Kingdom, a £159.98 listing at Argos is your best bet, besides a £161.18 option at Amazon UK that's imported from Europe with a slower delivery expectation.

  • Honeycomb Aeronautical Foxtrot Takeoff Kit (Black) at Walmart for $179.99

Otherwise, the standalone Foxtrot Aviation Stick is still available for $149.99 at Amazon US, though the compact Throttle Box isn't currently sold separately, so the Takeoff Kit bundle is a smarter buy. If you're unsure, or you're in another part of the world, Honeycomb lists more global resellers for extra options. Whichever you choose, the Foxtrot Takeoff Kit is only compatible with PC.

PC Only
Honeycomb Aeronautical Foxtrot Takeoff Kit: $179.99 at flyhoneycomb.com


"Designed for Microsoft Flight Simulator and X-Plane, it delivers smooth, precise control for both general aviation and airliner operations on PC and Mac."

View Listing

What I like about the Foxtrot Takeoff Kit

One of my only complaints from my review of the Foxtrot Aviation Stick was the lack of analog throttle controls, but that's what the compact Throttle Box is here to solve. Otherwise, the flight stick itself is identical, so everything I said in that original article is still accurate. That includes my willingness to settle for digital throttle control, but now I don't have to.

Underneath the Foxtrot stick, I spotted the same screw threads: a pair on either side. These finally have a use, since Honeycomb includes screws and plates that attach the Throttle Box to the left or right side of the Aviation Stick. That alone seriously improved my earliest experience with the Takeoff Kit, as the extra weight helps keep it grounded.

All four sliders feel identical, with enough resistance to stop them from rattling around or accidentally moving by small amounts. Each has a detent toward the bottom, which lets me push past into reverse thrust or lets me know when I'm at the limit for the speed brake and flaps. After a few flights, I found that I generally preferred a general aviation (GA) setup with propeller and mixture levers.

Along the bottom, four chunky switches come in adorably tiny versions of a landing gear lever, a pair of engine switches, and a rotating parking brake. I use them only a fraction as much as the sliders, but they still provide satisfyingly realistic feedback when I'm getting ready for take-off or completing a landing. Plus, I only needed to assign four axes and four buttons, so setup was fast.

Does the Foxtrot Takeoff Kit have any issues?

Image 1 of 2
Image 1 of 2

View Original
Image 2 of 2

View Original

The Foxtrot compact Throttle Box had two physical issues, though one was minor, and the other seems specific to my sample. That is, the interchangeable lever handles should be easy to swap out, but one doesn't fit flush because of an apparent fault in the plastic mould. So, if I wanted the complete GA set, I'd have to deal with a throttle lever that sits too high.

Sticking with the Airbus-style speed brake lever doesn't necessarily bother me too much, since it's the prop and mix handles that lean harder into the realism aspect, but it's something that would only be solved through a chat with Honeycomb's customer support team. There are no spare parts for sale on its website, so it's something to check when you buy the Foxtrot Takeoff Kit.

That minor issue is simply that the compact Throttle Box is too lightweight (~330g) to hold steady on my desk mat, sliding forward when I push the levers. It fares better on wood, giving the rubber feet a better chance to grip, but I suspect this might have influenced Honeycomb's decision not to sell it separately. Still usable, but it's better when tethered to the Aviation Stick.

So, the biggest downside to the Foxtrot Takeoff Kit is that the compact Throttle Box isn't sold separately, at least not yet. That might change in the future (and I hope that it does), but anyone who bought into the standalone Foxtrot Aviation Stick before now will be left feeling a little stuck.

In theory, the Throttle Box could retail for around $30, which hints at why it isn't available on its own. It could be that manufacturing costs are only covered when it's included as a bundle with the flightstick, and that mass-producing packaging and licensing for a separate unit isn't viable just yet.

On the other hand, Honeycomb already sells a range of accessories at a matching $29.99 price point, including a mix of electronics and plastic or metal add-ons. It's blocking existing consumers from accessing the most natural pairing for Honeycomb's Foxtrot stick, but it's less drastic for newcomers.

Otherwise, I'll always lament the lack of XBOX compatibility, but Honeycomb might solve that in the future with one of its 'XPC' variants. It delivered the same equivalents with its Alpha Flight Controls XPC, and an upcoming variant of its excellent Echo Aviation Controller is set to do the same.

Should you buy the Foxtrot Takeoff Kit?

You should buy this if ...

✅ You want an immersive flight sim experience

✅ You don't want an overwhelming setup with too many inputs

You should not buy this if ...

❌ You already own the Foxtrot Aviation Stick

Buying the Takeoff Kit gives you the fantastic Foxtrot Aviation Stick, which, while it doesn't feature the world's best technology, is still my favorite overall flightstick because it's so convenient. That's still the theme here, as Honeycomb adds a no-frills Throttle Box that mostly matches, but at the same time, feels like a more budget-grade add-on that should be sold (and branded) separately.

That, paired with an unfortunate flaw in the lever handles that came with my sample, leaves me wanting changes. If Honeycomb can sell the compact Throttle Box separately, with its own warranty support system, and even consider selling the GA lever handles separately, it'll win a higher score from me. Instead, it's easier to recommend the Bravo Throttle Quadrant Lite.

title: Xbox and PC prices are out of control, and Microsoft clearly knows it
author: Cale Hunt
summary: I used to upgrade my PC when it felt slow, but that's no longer possible because of rising hardware costs. Microsoft's strategy is evolving to meet this new reality, and two recent changes involving W...
content:
Microsoft's big news this week is about how Windows 11 is now considerably more responsive on 8GB of RAM. A couple of weeks ago, it was the Xbox Series X|S and AMD-powered gaming handhelds getting AMD's FSR 4.1 upscaling to help boost performance.

What do these stories have in common? To me, they're evidence that the standard tech market model is breaking down in the face of unprecedented hardware shortages.

Laptops and desktop PCs keep rising in price, even as they're stripped of memory and storage. Xbox consoles have never been pricier. The latest gaming handhelds, including the MSI Claw 8 EX AI+, are ballooning in price, to the point that they cost as much as a high-end gaming laptop from just a few years ago.

Consumer hardware that used to brute-force its way to acceptable performance in Windows, games, and beyond is no longer on the table for a lot of people because of AI-inflated prices.

What's left? Microsoft, despite its major role in the AI race, can't directly make hardware cheaper. It can, however, make it last longer by focusing on optimizations and innovations that offset the current economic reality that's keeping old hardware in our hands.

Windows 11 running better on 8GB PCs is part of a bigger picture

The bigger story surrounding Windows 11's 8GB improvements is that Microsoft is putting significant engineering efforts into improving the OS for low-end hardware. And it's not afraid to show it off.

To me, this is a reversal of tradition. For what feels like all my life until recently, the answer to a sluggish PC was to upgrade the hardware. Microsoft and its OEMs loved this tradition, of course, because it let them sell more products.

Now, the focus is shifting to making the hardware we have feel like it can indeed last until an upgrade becomes affordable.

This shift comes a couple of years after Microsoft's massive Copilot+ PC initiative, which I'm sure was conceived as an ultimate ploy to get users to buy new hardware.

That didn't turn out so well for Microsoft. The AI tools built into the OS failed to capture the whimsy of the average user. Adoption was slow, no doubt largely because of rising prices. The Copilot+ PC badge was eventually phased out in September 2026.

Microsoft must have realized at some point during this transition that the millions of Windows users still running old hardware are not going to upgrade any time soon.

Optimization used to be a nice bonus when it arrived, but it's now becoming a major pillar in Microsoft's consumer strategy.

AMD's FSR 4.1 will held extend the life of consoles and handhelds

Microsoft isn't just working on optimizations for Windows users. AMD recently announced it's bringing its FSR 4.1 upscaling technique to its older hardware, which includes Xbox Series X|S, Radeon RX 6000 GPUs, and a host of Ryzen-powered gaming handhelds, including the ROG Xbox Ally X.

I've discussed how this update gives the current console generation some much-needed legs in the face of next-gen uncertainty. It improves image quality, makes rendering easier, and boosts framerates (maybe not all at the same time).

It won't turn your Xbox into a supercomputer, but it is the next best thing to buying an entirely new device with more power. This is particularly important as rumors of the next-gen Xbox Helix's $1200-$1800 price begin to swirl.

If Helix indeed launches at that price, Microsoft has to know that adoption won't be fast. But the company also knows it can't afford to lose those Xbox gamers.

Keeping the Series X|S relevant longer into the future ensures that gamers keep buying Game Pass subscriptions, keep buying new games, and, ultimately, remain inside the ecosystem.

Microsoft doesn't really need people to buy new PCs

Microsoft used to make ungodly amounts of money from licensing Windows on PCs. However, it's arrived at a point where licenses are a tiny fraction of revenue. It's all about the subscriptions now, including Game Pass, Microsoft 365, OneDrive, Copilot, Azure, and many more.

Don't get me wrong; I'm sure Microsoft would still love to be selling a ton of PCs. That's just good for business. That's not what's happening these days. PC sales are on a steep decline because of rising prices.

But as long as people are still using some sort of Windows PC that doesn't frustrate them with sluggish performance, there's a good chance that Microsoft will receive at least one monthly payment and remain within the ecosystem.

The current upgrade cycle is stuck in place

Microsoft realized at some point that the upgrade cycle we're currently in is going to last for a lot longer than usual, especially as prices keep climbing.

And although I'm sure there were external circumstances playing a role in these recent optimizations I laid out, the big story is that Microsoft knows software is the answer to unaffordable hardware.

Do you agree with my opinions above? Do you think we'll be seeing a lot more software optimization in the years to come if PC prices don't drop? Do you think this is all just a small bandage on a seeping wound? Let me know in the comments section below!

title: MW4 DMZ players need to do this loot run before Season 1 starts
author: Richard Devine
summary: Solo players who don't have a lot of time to play Modern Warfare 4 DMZ may feel like they're not getting enough good loot. But that changes with this easy run that takes less than 15 minutes each time...
content:
Season 1 is coming to Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 on November 6, a mere two weeks after it officially launched. For DMZ players, there will be a bunch of new content, not least the new X01 map.

But I get it; you may also feel like you're 'behind' or not prepared. You see the big content creators on Twitch and YouTube with a stash full of the highest rarity items. But most of us aren't able to play the game all day (even I, when covering it is part of my job).

Solo players can also feel a little left out, since regularly hitting the toughest areas for the best gear usually needs the coordination of a full squad. X01 especially sounds like it's going to be tough, so you're going to want gear. And plenty of weapons.

Fortunately, even if you are playing solo, there are some good routes out there you can run with the sole purpose of just getting loot. And decent loot, at that. The one I'm going to feature here can be done in 10-15 minutes, has an exfil close by every time, and crucially, should be pretty chilled out.

How to farm good loot and weapons in MW4 DMZ easily as a solo player

I take no credit for coming up with this idea. Plenty of folks on YouTube have talked about it, and I first saw TheSpazo on YouTube recommend it as a loot run.

You may like
  • How to use blueprints to get high-tier weapons in Modern Warfare 4 DMZ
  • We've finally got some actual details on Modern Warfare 4's DMZ mode
  • How to get the parachute in Modern Warfare 4 DMZ

Essentially we're going to target six bunkers on the left side of the map and throw in one compound that sits on the route. This guarantees six weapon lockers and a safe, as well as plenty of bags, military lockers, foot lockers, tool boxes, and, if you need to upgrade your FOB, a ton of valuables really easily.

The first thing you need to do is deploy into the Operation Iron Citadel story mission. If you don't have this unlocked yet, you need to complete the first three missions on the pyramid and you'll get access.

You don't need to do the mission for this, but using it guarantees you're going to spawn on the map in the right place.

Image 1 of 6
Image 1 of 6

Image 2 of 6

Image 3 of 6

Image 5 of 6

View Original

When you're in your raid, open the map, and you're looking for six marks along the left portion that are little circles. They're missile silos, which may come into play in future content, but attached to them are bunkers full of goodies.

There will be one to the west of where you spawn, so hit that one first. There will then be a second one south of that. The gallery above shows all the grid locations for each of the six.

What to read next
  • Make sure you have the RIGHT backpack to protect your loot in MW4 DMZ
  • What you need to know about the Forward Operating Base in MW4 DMZ
  • I tested MW4’s new DMZ mode, and the experience was way stranger (and better) than expected

Basically you need to grab the first vehicle you can and hit all six bunkers as fast as possible. A car will often spawn near you when you load in, or you can find one down at Deadtown.

But the route is simple. Start at the bottom around where you spawn, drive up to each silo, go in through the bunker entrance that will be off to one side, and just loot everything inside.

You'll find maybe one AI enemy in some of the bunkers, but that's about the only resistance. When you come to a door locked from the inside, simply follow the windows and go round to the door at the other side of the room. This is the room you really want to hit because it's where you'll find the weapon lockers.

The only non-bunker part of this run is the Military Compound just north of the airbase. You don't need to waste time clearing it; simply approach from the south, go through the gap in the wall, up the external staircase on the first building, and the safe is in the room at the top.

Then leave the way you came and go back to hitting the bunkers. By the time you finish, you'll have had a chance to loot at least six weapons along with a ton of other great stuff.

The valuables you get are also an easy way to get DMZ Cash by selling them in the FOB. If you're not needing any to craft upgrades, just sell them, and you'll be rolling in cash. Maybe hang onto any Gold Skulls or Gold Bars, though if you find any, because you'll need them at some point in the future, and they're pretty darn rare.

Once you've looted all the bunkers, hit an exfil and get out. If your Operator has the Trait that reveals the Final Exfil point on the map, this will often be in the top left corner, which is ideal to hit from the final bunker.

Other players in your match are less likely to be there, but if it's not, there always seems to be an exfil in the vicinity of the airbase if you've loaded in via the story mission.

There's the whole discussion over whether there are actually fewer players in a lobby when you select a story mission or not, but in my experience this run has been pretty chilled. I've only seen one player in the last 10 runs, funnily enough, someone who beat me to the Final Exfil point.

So you do need to keep your guard up, but only you will spawn at that location for that story mission, so it increases your odds. But speed is of the essence. Don't waste time running; don't waste time looting other buildings. Get a vehicle and move fast, in and out.

Take a Weapon Backpack if you have one

As you're focusing on just harvesting loot with this run, you want to take as little as possible in with you. You shouldn't be coming into contact with many enemies, so one tip would be to only take in one weapon so you have a vacant slot.

If you have a Weapon Backpack you can use, take it, because with a vacant slot in your loadout and this, you have a chance to exfil with two new weapons per run.

At the very least use a Medium Backpack if you can, because that secure slot will guarantee you get out with any high-value items you find, such as recipes and weapon manuals.

But leave your backpack as empty as possible. You need the space because you're going to find a lot of loot.

I specifically say this is a good loot run to carry out as many times as you can before Season 1 for a couple of reasons.

The first is that right now, choosing this story mission seems to have reverted to the old ways where there seem to be fewer players. Only one person will ever get a story mission spawn at a time, so you will be starting on your own. But still, other players exist, so speed is essential.

The other reason is that this could change when Season 1 starts. Or loot spawns could change. In a live service mode like DMZ, always be ready for a change to come in that could end whatever methods you've become comfortable with. But we've had the final pre-season update now (as far as we know) so you have at least a few days while it should stay like this.

So it's a good time to stock up on weapons and materials and get crafting FOB upgrades if you can. Especially if you're wanting to check out X01. That promises to be a difficult location, so get the best start you can before it arrives.

title: Excel copy and paste breaks once again after Microsoft update
author: Sean Endicott
summary: Microsoft has shipped another Excel 2016 update that breaks copy and paste, marking the second consecutive month with the same issue.
content:
Copying and pasting continues to be an issue for those who install the latest updates from Microsoft. Just one month after an update broke functionality in Excel, October's release has caused the same issue.

The latest issues are caused by the KB5002934 update for Microsoft Excel, which is for Excel 2016. That version replaces KB5002665, which included a hotfix for a copy/paste bug. Despite superseding the previous update, the KB5002934 update can also prevent you from copying and pasting if a workbook contains conditional formatting.

Only a small set of Excel users should be affected by the bug, since it's limited to Excel 2016. Newer versions of Excel do not have the issue.

Latest Videos FromWindows Central

The bug appears in a way that may confuse those who run into it. Rather than Excel showing an error message or making a noise, the function simply fails.

The updates to Excel ship through Windows Update, though they aren't updates to the operating system itself. They function similarly to updates for other Microsoft apps such as Edge.

You may like
  • Microsoft addresses Excel’s copy/paste regression but the fix barely reaches most users
  • Windows 11's buggy September continues, this time breaking a key Excel feature
  • Outlook and Teams are down for Surface and Windows on ARM users after a regression

Luckily for those facing the issue, Microsoft has already fixed the bug. The company released a new build of Excel that fixes the issue. If Excel is running build 16.0.5574.1006 (or later), you should be fine.

You can check your Excel version by opening File > Account and looking under About Excel.

If for some reason you are still facing the issue, you can try these steps from Microsoft as a workaround:

  • On the Home tab, select the Paste dropdown list, and then select Paste Special.
  • In the Paste Special window, select one of the following options:
    • Formulas
    • Formulas & Number Formatting
    • Values
    • Values & Number Formatting
    • Link

I'm glad that Microsoft fixed the problem so quickly, but it's concerning that updates caused the same issues two months in a row.

title: WH40K: Rogue Trader's final DLC expansion is coming soon — and it looks amazing
author: Alexander Cope
summary: Owlcat Games has revealed the release date of Warhammer 40,000: Rogue Trader's final DLC expansion, "Processional of the Damned". It will feature a new playable companion, a new "Zealot" player archet...
content:
Warhammer 40,000: Rogue Trader, one of my favorite RPGs in years, is releasing its final DLC expansion, "Processional of the Damned", on December 8, 2026, for Xbox Series X|S, PlayStation 5, Nintendo Switch 2, and PC via Steam, GOG, and the Epic Games Store.

It will feature a brand new storyline, a new party member, a new "Zealot" archetype, new enemies to battle, new gameplay features, new gear, and much more.

Here's what you need to know about the "Processional of the Damned" DLC.

Warhammer 40,000: Rogue Trader | Final DLC Release Date Announcement Trailer - YouTube
Watch On

The expansion will have players meet a recruitable companion named Stella, a miraculist raised by the Order of Saint Cognatius.

She leads you on a trip across the galaxy to explore a giant voidship graveyard infamously known as the "Processional of the Damned" due to a mysterious force calling her there.

Things get dicey quickly as you and your crew get trapped within the voidship graveyard. Now must work with the survivors of a lost missionary expedition to uncover the Processional of the Damned's mysteries, learn what drew Stella to this accursed place, and find a way to escape before the Forces of Chaos or worse things slaughter you.

As this is Warhammer 40,000: Rogue Trader's last DLC expansion, it's going all out with tons of new gameplay features, including:

  • Stella, a new Miraculist companion who can set enemies on fire with psychic Pyromancy and change their abilities mid-fight depending on Veil Degradation or how many Psykers there are currently in your party.
  • A playable "Zealot" archetype that's all about smashing enemies to death with hammers and other bludgeoning melee weapons.
  • New enemies to fight, including Chaos Space Marines from the Black Legion and Aeldari from the Iyanden Craftworld.
  • A new "Insanity" gameplay mechanic that will inflict horrifying effects on all of your companions, especially Stella.
  • New weapons (including a Grenade Launcher), a new romance option, new companion events, new items, new space exploration options, and other hidden surprises.

I'm going to miss this wonderfully dark and amazing RPG take on WH40K

Out of all the RPGs I've played these past few years, I've never been so enthralled by one as much as Warhammer 40,000: Rogue Trader. Not only was it the best introduction to Warhammer 40,000's vast, complex universe lore for newcomers, but it's also a brilliant game in its own right.

Its characters had rich personalities with intriguing arcs; its turn-based tactical combat was brutal and satisfying; its storylines had me hooked from beginning to end, and its vast array of dialogue choices had meaningful consequences while vastly improving replay value.

On top of that, every expansion released for Warhammer 40,000: Rogue Trader was jam-packed with amazing content that aimed to make the whole game better, rather than just a few extra bits here and there.

So I can't wait to see what insane final adventures Owlcat Games has in store for us when Warhammer 40,000: Rogue Trader's Processional of the Damned DLC expansion launches on December 8, 2026.

Whatever it is, it will be a great way to kill time while waiting for Warhammer 40,000: Rogue Trader's successor, Warhammer 40,000: Dark Heresy, to come out next year.

title: Microsoft is tackling Outlook's search problem, and it wants your feedback
author: Sean Endicott
summary: Microsoft revamped Outlook search with better ranking, improved performance, and a new feedback system that lets users rate results.
content:
Searching for a specific email in Outlook can prove challenging. Outlook search can sometimes return irrelevant results while missing the exact email you need. Microsoft is looking to improve that frustrating experience with a revamped search.

The new search has a feature that genuinely removes the most frustrating part of Outlook for me. That phrase is thrown around a lot online and is often clickbait, but I mean it here emphatically.

Outlook now handles stop words better. Those words, such as "the," "and," and "is," often clog search results with irrelevant emails. I can't tell you how many times those tiny words have led to terrible searches that made me fish through the results that appear chronologically.

Latest Videos FromWindows Central

Microsoft's example from a blog post shows how drastically different the results are when searching "the FY27 budget" using the old Outlook search versus the new one.

The improvements highlighted by Microsoft center around ranking emails better. Microsoft focused on three areas when building the new search tool in Outlook: better ranking, improved performance when connectivity is poor, and a tighter feedback loop.

You may like
  • Windows 11’s Search overhaul is coming fast — here’s what you really need to know
  • Microsoft's 'classic' skin is a band-aid for the new Outlook's awful UI
  • New Outlook will soon check emails for spelling mistakes before they are sent

When you search for an email within Outlook, you will see seven ranked results rather than three. Those emails are ranked based on recency, sender, how much the message has been interacted with, and other factors. Expanding the number of ranked messages presented should show users more relevant emails while also helping Microsoft improve its ranking systems over time.

The new ranking layout is available across several versions of Outlook, including the new and Classic versions.

There are other upgrades as well. Classic Outlook now automatically falls back to locally indexed content when connectivity is poor. That same functionality is on the way to new Outlook but will ship later.

Users of Classic Outlook should also see faster search results. Microsoft also said recent improvements reduced latency for the slowest 5% of Outlook searches.

The improved rankings in Outlook are the result of a small language model ranker built specifically for Outlook. That model is trained through distillation, meaning it is built under the supervision of a larger model.

Distillation helps Outlook search be more efficient than if it had to run a larger model just to look through and rank emails.

I'd probably be okay with using a larger model in Outlook if it cut out irrelevant results that appear simply for using an article or common verb like "is." I bet I'd still save some time that way. But I don't have to test that theory because the new Outlook search is lightweight.

title: Halo Wars Meets Halo: Reach in this Impressive FPS Mod
author: Adam Hales
summary: Project Groundside brings first-person combat to Halo Wars, allowing players to take direct control of Marines, Spartans, ODSTs, and vehicles. Inspired by Halo: Reach, the mod introduces new weapons, ...
content:
If you’re like me, a massive Halo fan, you’ve probably played Halo Wars at some point. Maybe you enjoyed the huge battles with friends online, or perhaps you just stuck to the campaign because, well, it was great. But have you ever found yourself thinking how cool it would be to get your feet on the ground and see it all from a first-person perspective? Well, now you can.

Researching this has been a bit of a headache. It’s been difficult to pin down who originally created the crossover, but from what I can tell, there are at least two projects out there? Both presumably use AI to achieve the first-person mode, because that’s just the world we live in now.

The two projects in question are Halo: Theater of War and Project Groundside. For the sake of simplicity, I’m going to focus on Project Groundside, since it appears to be the main project people are using and playing. If you’d like to try it yourself, you can join their Discord server linked here.

Just a quick heads up too: these mods are only available on PC, so if you're on console, you're sadly out of luck.

Project Groundside turns Halo Wars into a first-person shooter

Halo: Project Groundside (Fan Project) - YouTube
Watch On

Project Groundside lets you play Halo Wars normally, but with the ability to control units in first person. The style is heavily inspired by Halo: Reach, complete with Reach weapon models and a sprint mechanic. In fact, you can even drive a Warthog, tank, and Falcon, and there’s a third-person mode available too.

  • Halo 3 inside Fallout: New Vegas is the latest entry in gaming’s “nothing makes sense anymore” era
  • Halo 5: Reforged is an unofficial community effort that brings the game to PC

The project also introduces a respawn mechanic where you can choose to load in as a Marine, Spartan, or ODST, each with different weapons to choose from. Respawns do cost supplies, though, to try and keep things balanced.

Now, this mod serves more as a proof of concept, but it’s pretty cool nonetheless. With the future of Halo up in the air, it’s refreshing to see projects like this give fans a taste of something different, especially when nobody knows how long it'll be till the next game.

I, for one, would love to see large-scale battles in a Halo sandbox with destructible environments in an official game. We’re sort of getting a glimpse of that with modded Halo 3 on PC, which has up to 128 players now in a match, and that's definitely tiding me over for now.

title: If you skipped Windows 11’s 2026 update over bugs, Microsoft has now fixed all...
author: Abhijith M B
summary: Weeks after September's update broke File History, Remote Desktop and File Explorer, Microsoft's 25H2 status page tells users to move to 26H2. We break down every fix from KB5129195 to KB5127936, the ...
content:
To everyone holding on to last year’s OS version, Microsoft’s Windows 11 25H2 status page now says, “We recommend updating to version 26H2 to stay up to date, secure, and productive.” On the 26H2 status page, four of the five tracked known issues are now marked resolved, except a USB audio bug, which Microsoft shows as mitigated.

The recommendation comes after a rough couple of months. 26H2 rolled out on September 29, just weeks after the September update broke multiple features, and it launched with three known issues already active. A month later, Windows 11 is in far better shape (including performance!)

Microsoft has fixed four of Windows 11 26H2’s five known issues

The September 8 update, KB5124008, broke Remote Desktop sessions, crashed File Explorer, and quietly stopped File History backups, accompanied by a false and strange “Reconnect your drive” warning. Microsoft’s explanation for the Explorer crashes was that “The September Windows updates were extensive.” Well, that’s one way to put it.

Microsoft needed four updates to squash the bug, starting with an emergency patch, KB5129195, on September 14. File History backups started working again with the October 2026 Patch Tuesday update in our testing, and the last fix came on October 28 with KB5127936. The table shows the current condition of the 26H2 status page:

Known issue Status Fixed by
Remote Desktop fails for non-admin users (error 0xC000000D) Resolved KB5127936, October 28
Black screen or desktop loading issues after sign-in Resolved KB5127648, October 13
Apps close during AC-3 audio decoding Resolved KB5127648, October 13
Domain-joined devices lose trust with the domain Resolved KB5124010, September 22
USB Audio Class 1.0 devices fail or produce no sound Mitigated Partial fix in KB5129195, September 14

 

USB audio is the one Windows 11 26H2 bug Microsoft hasn’t fixed

“After installing Windows 11, version 26H2, some USB Audio Class 1.0 devices might fail to start or produce audio,” Microsoft says. If your device is on that unfortunate list, it may show a Code 10 error, produce no sound, or the volume controls and sound settings may become unresponsive. USB Audio Class 1.0 is the older, driverless standard that is still used by a lot of USB headsets, microphones, and DACs.

Microsoft’s September 14 emergency update fixed the 8-channel and 3D audio symptoms, so the company marks the bug as mitigated, not resolved. For everything else, the company says, “We are working to address this issue in a future Windows update and will provide more information when it is available.” The entry hasn’t been updated since September 29.

Also, in case you’re wondering, skipping 26H2 won’t protect you here, as Microsoft lists the bug on every Windows 11 version from 23H2 onwards, Windows 10 22H2, and even Windows Server 2012.

Skipping Windows 11 26H2 won’t save you from bugs, and delaying updates is riskier than ever

Windows 11 26H2 isn’t a new operating system. Microsoft’s enablement package documentation says, “Windows 11, versions 24H2, 25H2, and 26H2 share a common core operating system with an identical set of system files,” and the new features “remain dormant until they are turned on.” That’s why the upgrade needs just a single restart, and why a bug in one version usually shows up in all three, as Microsoft explained when 26H2 launched.

I wouldn’t dare delay monthly updates, either. In September, Microsoft 365 director Jeremy Chapman said Microsoft cut its recommended window for deploying Windows updates to “less than three days,” as anything longer is “ample time for attackers using AI to find and exploit known security gaps.” October’s Patch Tuesday fixed a record 1,413 vulnerabilities, including a Windows Shell flaw that was already being exploited. If you’re on 24H2 Home or Pro, support ended on October 13, so the upgrade isn’t optional anymore.

There’s a performance reason, too. Microsoft’s latest 8GB RAM improvements, which make Windows up to 20% more responsive on those PCs, need 26H2 build 26300.9818 or later. When I updated my own 16GB laptop to 26H2, RAM usage after a restart fell by as much as 2GB, and my dad’s 8GB laptop dropped from 5GB to 3.3GB. I would say update to 26H2 just for the performance benefits.

To upgrade, open Settings > Windows Update and click Check for updates. “If Windows 11, version 26H2 is available for your device, select Download & install,” Microsoft says (proudly, I presume).

Windows 11 26H2 is ready for most people

I’ve been on 26H2 since early October, and Windows 11 feels better now than it has in a long time. Credit where it’s due, Microsoft cleaned up most of September’s mess in about seven weeks.

But “recommended” doesn’t mean bug-free, and if your USB headset or DAC is acting up, Redmond is still on it. Have you moved to Windows 11 26H2 yet?

title: GIMP 3.2.8 released with improved text tool, performance
author: OMG! Ubuntu!
content:
GIMP 3.2.8 is out, the fourth maintenance update in the current stable series, which first launched in March 2026.

No shiny new features ship, as fixes and fine-tuning are the primary focus. Major work is happening alongside maintenance efforts, but that work is targeted at the next major series.

What’s changed since the v3.2.6 update in September?

GIMP 3.2.8 offers better initial positioning of dialogs, makes the Preferences page load faster and allows the creation of colourful semi-transparent borders via the Add Border filter.

This update also bolsters the text tool’s support for right-to-left (RTL) languages. Arrow keys behave correctly and direction icons show on the on-canvas UI. If text direction isn’t set, the Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm picks one based on the first character typed.

A “gotcha” was fixed when editing linked layer files (GIMP’s version of Photoshop’s Smart Objects). The attributes dialog no longer allows clicking OK while a linked file is in the process of being added. Cancel remains selectable, if needed.

Performance tweaks bring better caching for large gradients (6000px) and a more efficient “marching ants” animation. HEIF loading code was tweaked to allow for loading larger images.

For its developers, a new GUI testing suite was added. The team says this will help them check for regressions in the GUI during development, rather than after. It plans to share more details on that soon.

Beyond that, the v3.2.8 update delivers a pinch of platform-specific fixes for GIMP’s macOS and Windows versions, including better theme matching, printing and windowing behaviour.

Besides simply being all-round a bit better, this update is a bit safer too. A small set of security updates are rolled in, plugging a few recently discovered vulnerabilities in libraries GIMP uses.

A tame release? Obviously; it’s maintenance update.

With enthusiasm for Affinity’s planned Linux release, AI-sired Adobe clones and emerging projects is high, it’s easy to forget that FOSS tools already exist and are already capable of doing wonderful, creative things.

Get GIMP 3.2.8

Download the latest version of The GIMP from the official website. It has Linux AppImages, as well as official installers for Windows and macOS installers. All are available for 64-bit Intel/AMD and 64-bit ARM devices.

Alternatively, GIMP is available on Flathub and on the Snap Store. Windows users can get it from the Microsoft Store too. If installed from a vendor store, this update will be made available delivered there, so remember to check.

title: Canonical adds FIDO2 hardware key support to Launchpad
author: OMG! Ubuntu!
content:
Developers who use Launchpad can now use a USB FIDO2 security key to restrict API access, which makes any stolen login details useless without it.

Launchpad is, as I’m sure you know, where Canonical builds Ubuntu’s package, hosts code, PPAs and many other things that end up on a users’ system.

Developer tools, like lp-shell and ubuntu-archive-tools, log in with a saved token, normally kept as a text file or in the desktop keyring on the developer’s machine. Anyone who gets hold of it, malware included, could act as them, with the permissions it carries.

Canonical’s Jürgen Gmach says “for most people that is an acceptable risk”. For core distro dev, engineers and package uploaders? Well, they have more to lose and could become a ‘tempting target’ for bad actors (not the Tommy Wiseau kind).

Which is why Launchpad has added support for hardware-bound API tokens.

These replace the stored token with “a long-lived OAuth refresh grant” that can’t do much without the physical security key attached. Logging in requires touching the key and entering its pin. This issues a short-lived token for everyday requests.

The key protects the stored grant, so malware that ran with the developer logged in could still use any short-lived token for its (brief) lifetime, but it wouldn’t be able to request a new one.

Developers wanting to opt-in will need a supported device (only USB keys are supported; NFC keys and passkeys stored on a device are not) and the python3-fido2 package installed.

Full setup details are listed in the launchpadlib docs.

title: Microsoft’s own video show how badly Windows 11 struggled on 8GB RAM PCs, and...
author: Mayank Parmar
summary: Microsoft has declared that you can "do more with 8GB ," and this time, these are not just words, as the changes are already available. If you use Windows 11 26H2 or newer, Microsoft...
content:
Microsoft has declared that you can “do more with 8GB [of RAM],” and this time, these are not just words, as the changes are already available. If you use Windows 11 26H2 or newer, Microsoft says your system can be up to 40% more responsive, and the improvements are mostly visible on PCs with 8GB of RAM.

Microsoft spent the last two years convincing regular users that they need at least 16GB of RAM, and gamers that 32GB of RAM is a “must” for serious players.

RAM prices are through the roof, and Microsoft is now selling PCs with 8GB of RAM again. Its OEM partners have also started building and selling 8GB RAM PCs to take on the MacBook Neo, which runs comparatively better than Windows 11 with fewer resources, but that has finally begun changing.

It’s not that Windows isn’t doing better on a PC with 32GB of RAM, but the optimizations are obviously more noticeable on low-end PCs.

In a test on two PCs with 8GB of RAM, Microsoft opened 20 tabs in the Edge browser, played a 4K video, and opened a Word document, a PowerPoint presentation, Excel, Outlook, and File Explorer.

Now, the first PC is running Windows 11’s January 2026 update, which predates Microsoft’s commitments from March 2026. And you’ve got a second PC with Windows 11 26H2 (October 2026 Update).

In both tests, Microsoft does exactly the same thing. It opens Edge sites (fake brands like Contoso, VanArsdel, Northwind, Adatum, and Fourth Coffee), File Explorer, the right-click menu, PowerPoint, Excel, and Word.

While the October machine is clearly finishing everything first, you’d notice that the January version of Windows was really a mess, as it would often get stuck on a blank or loading window while the October one had already moved on to the next app.

“Tested on identical Windows PCs with Windows 11 OS 26200.7623 compared to 26200.9445; actual results vary by device, configuration, app version, usage, and other factors. Footage accelerated for time,” Microsoft noted.

This doesn’t mean you shouldn’t see any changes if your hardware is different from the undisclosed device of Microsoft, but do not blindly expect 20% less RAM usage or 40% more responsiveness after recent updates.

Up to 40% faster response times on the same 8GB PC after the October 2026 update

Now, on the same hardware, Microsoft says Windows is far more responsive, and the improvements can go well above 40% on certain configurations.

This claim is based on response times for Search, Start, right-click, Settings, Snipping Tool, and File Explorer on PCs with 8GB of memory. Microsoft compared Windows 11 Build 26300.9550 (26H2) with OS Build 26200.7628 (25H2).

However, Microsoft warns that “rollout timing and availability may vary by device and region,” so these changes may not be live for everyone yet.

I believe these are related to Low Latency Profile (LLP), which uses your CPU for brief bursts of performance to make Windows feel far more responsive.

Also, if you watch the video closely, you’d notice that the “less committed memory” figure grows as each app is added:

  • Teams: 375 MB
  • PowerPoint: 612 MB
  • Edge: 794 MB
  • Word: 869 MB
  • Excel: 891 MB
  • Outlook: 900 MB

Microsoft says it calculated these numbers “based on changes in measured system-committed memory from baseline to final state during multitasking with Edge, Office, Outlook, and Teams.”

Finally, Microsoft argues that these apps now use up to 900 MB less committed memory compared to January 2026, which is a pretty big deal for a PC with just 8GB of RAM.

Most of these improvements are already live, so if you don’t notice a difference, your PC may not have been the bottleneck Microsoft targeted. As I said, it’s mostly noticeable on 8GB RAM PCs, but if you’ve got a low-end processor, that 40% responsiveness may be off the table due to less impact of Low Latency Profile.

title: Russian Police Arrest 3 Suspected VasyGrek Hackers, Dismantle Criminal Infrastructure
author: The Hacker News

content:
Russian authorities have arrested three suspected members of a threat group known as VasyGrek and dismantled its criminal infrastructure.

Also known as Fluffy Wolf, the threat actor has a history of targeting Russian and international companies since 2016.

The Ministry of Internal Affairs of the Russian Federation (MVD) said members of the group are "suspected of embezzling funds from the accounts of organizations, as well as creating, distributing, and using malicious software."

In one September 2025 case highlighted by the ministry, the attackers are said to have sent a phishing email to an unnamed organization, masquerading it as business correspondence and instructing recipients to open a reconciliation report that triggered the execution of malware.

The incident resulted in losses of 660,000 rubles ($8,000) from the organization's bank account, with the attackers transferring the funds to accounts under their control.

"The attacks utilized a vast network of phishing domains imitating financial and accounting service websites, as well as virtual servers located in foreign countries," MVD said. "Tools for covert remote administration were acquired from the dark web."

The rare law enforcement action saw Russian authorities conducting searches at the suspects' residences and the office premises they used to conduct the operations. It also led to the seizure of computer equipment, communication devices, and other items of evidentiary value.

According to reports from Russian cybersecurity company BI.ZONE and F6, VasyGrek is assessed to be a financially motivated threat actor that gains initial access by sending phishing emails with attachments disguised as financial documents.

Some of the key tools in its arsenal include off-the-shelf stealers and trojans, like MetaStealer, PureCrypter, PureLogs Stealer, WarZone RAT, XMRig, BurnsRAT, PureHVNC, PureRAT, Pay2Key, and PowerLoader, as well as legitimate remote access software such as Remote Utilities.

In a report published this week, Kaspersky said it recorded over 100 attempted attacks orchestrated by VasyGrek against organizations in Russia, Belarus, and Kazakhstan between January and September 2026. These attacks have also been observed using decoy documents to drop a Golang backdoor capable of executing arbitrary commands on the infected device.

The attacks primarily singled out entities in the metallurgical sector, along with wholesale suppliers of raw materials and industrial supplies and government agencies. Other targets included organizations in the healthcare, oil and gas, energy, finance, and agriculture sectors.

"The group expanded its attack geography: while previously its primary target was Russian organizations, this year, potential victims also included companies from Belarus and Kazakhstan," Nikita Nazarov, head of advanced threat research at Kaspersky, said.

"The attackers used multi-stage infection schemes and legitimate online services to host malicious components, which helped conceal their activity and hinder attack analysis."

The development comes as BI.ZONE it detected multiple attacks targeting Russian organizations using malware families like LxBase RAT, CoreRAT, and NightStrike RAT.

While LxBase RAT, a commercial trojan that costs $119 per month, is distributed via mass phishing campaigns, CoreRAT infection chains make use of phishing emails containing 7zSFX and Rust droppers for delivery. The activity has been attributed to Core Werewolf, which is assessed to share some level of overlap with Vortex Werewolf.

Attacks deploying NightStrike RAT have been associated with a hacktivist-turned-cyber espionage cluster dubbed Insolent Werewolf. Initial access is achieved using ClickFix-style attacks to deploy NetSupport Manager to gain remote access.

"Insolent Werewolf also utilizes Octowave Loader to deploy AdaptixC2 and Havoc post‑exploitation framework implants in compromised systems," BI.ZONE said, adding the group's malware arsenal includes other remote access trojans like CapDoor and NightWire.

"A RAT written in C++, NightStrike has presumably been created by the developer of NightWire, based on similarities in coding style. Utilizing diverse frameworks and their own custom malware allows the adversary to tailor tooling to specific attack conditions and reduce the likelihood of detection."

content:
A flaw in APT, the package manager for Debian and Ubuntu, allows an attacker who can modify package downloads to swap a checked package for their own.

The attacker's code then runs as root, according to advisories that Debian, Ubuntu, and APT's developers published on November 4. The attack needs APT to retry failed downloads, which it does by default from Debian 12 and Ubuntu 22.04 onward.

Debian has released fixed versions of APT for the flaw, CVE-2026-109518. APT's developers, who call the flaw critical, say updates for Ubuntu and its Ubuntu Pro subscription service are being released. Ubuntu 14.04 users with Ubuntu Pro can already get one.

Older releases, such as Debian 11 and Ubuntu 20.04, are not exposed by default, according to Ubuntu. But many user scripts may have turned on the retry setting, Acquire::Retries, on those releases anyway, APT's developers say.

Debian's testing branch was still on the vulnerable version 3.3.5 at 14:58 UTC on November 4. For Debian 11, whose Debian long-term support ended on August 31, APT's developers have published a fixed version, 2.2.5.

Ubuntu rates the flaw as high priority, with a CVSS 4.0 score of 7.7, and says that distributions built on Debian and Ubuntu are affected as well, without naming any.

Ubuntu published new APT builds for four of its releases to its security archive at 14:25 UTC on November 4:

  • Ubuntu 26.10: 3.3.3ubuntu0.1
  • Ubuntu 26.04 LTS: 3.2.1ubuntu0.1
  • Ubuntu 24.04 LTS: 2.8.4ubuntu0.1
  • Ubuntu 22.04 LTS: 2.4.15ubuntu0.1

At 15:46 UTC, Ubuntu still marked all eight releases it tracks for the flaw, from 14.04 LTS to 26.10, as vulnerable.

The attacker can be anyone who can change the HTTP traffic between APT and the package server, including a malicious mirror or proxy, according to Ubuntu. The attack runs when the computer installs a package. The attacker uses HTTP redirects and ordinary temporary server errors to make APT retry the download, APT's developers say.

Max Justicz reported the flaw. None of the three advisory reports describe attacks exploiting the flaw or offer a workaround for systems that cannot update yet. They describe the attack over HTTP and do not say whether package sources reached over HTTPS are exposed.

content:
A critical Android flaw could allow an attacker to run code on a phone without any user action remotely, Google said in its November security bulletin.

The flaw, CVE-2026-58868, affects Android 14 through 17. Phones get the fix with security patch level 2026-11-01 or later, which phone makers and carriers send on their own schedules.

As of November 4, Google's bulletin did not report any attacks exploiting its flaws. None of them was in the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, kept by the U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, as of its November 3 update.

The flaw is a possible out-of-bounds write caused by a heap buffer overflow in the onOutputReceived function of the file FrameDecoder.cpp. Neither the bulletin nor the flaw's CVE record says how an attacker would reach that code.

Google's Critical rating assumes that the protections built into Android and Google's services are turned off or bypassed.

Older versions, such as Android 12 and 13, are not listed as affected by the flaw. Google's records do not say whether they contain it.

How to Check Your Phone

Google's help page gives these steps:

  1. Open the Settings app.
  2. Tap About phone, or About tablet, then Android version.
  3. Find the dates for the Android security update and the Google Play system update.

The Android security update date is the phone's security patch level. A date of 2026-11-01 or later covers CVE-2026-58868 and the other flaws in the Framework, System, and Android runtime components.

A date of 2026-11-05 or later covers every flaw in the November bulletin, including those in the kernel and in parts from Arm, Imagination Technologies, MediaTek, Unisoc and Qualcomm.

Google sets two dates so phone makers can ship a set of fixes common to all Android devices sooner. It encourages them to include every fix in the bulletin.

Phones running Android 10 or later may also receive some fixes through Google Play system updates. This month's list for those updates includes another Critical flaw, CVE-2026-58876.

CVE-2026-58868 is not on that list, so the date to check for it is the Android security update.

The bulletin gives no workaround for phones that cannot install the update yet.

A Remote Denial-of-Service Flaw in Android's Text-Message Code

Another Critical flaw, CVE-2026-58882, could allow a remote denial-of-service attack with no user interaction, according to its CVE record. It is in decodeWapPdu, a function in Android's code for WAP Push messages that arrive via SMS.

On October 29, a researcher who publishes as Mark B posted a write-up called "SMS of Death" about a bug in the same function. Neither the bulletin nor the CVE record says whether CVE-2026-58882 is that bug.

One malformed WAP Push message crashes com.android.phone and ends any active call, including emergency calls, according to the write-up. In tests on several phone models, the crash happened every time.

The attacker needs only the target's phone number, and the message never shows up in the inbox. The phone retries the message each time it starts, so it can crash on startup until the message is removed.

A proof-of-concept app that sends such a message from one phone to another is public. Phones running Android 12 and 13 run the same code but do not receive the fix that newer versions do, the researcher says.

Other Critical Flaws

Google's November bulletin lists 216 vulnerabilities, 23 of them rated Critical. Two more Critical flaws could allow remote code execution: CVE-2026-58876 and CVE-2026-58936, both in Android's System component.

Six Critical flaws are in the kernel, two of them in Bluetooth code. The most severe kernel flaw could allow a remote attacker to gain elevated privileges without user interaction.

The 2026-11-05 patch level also fixes Critical flaws in MediaTek modem code and in a closed-source Qualcomm component. In its November bulletin, MediaTek describes its Critical modem flaws as out-of-bounds writes and says it is not aware of any active exploitation.

content:
SonicWall has warned of two vulnerabilities impacting end-of-life Global Management System (GMS) systems that it said will not be patched.

Details of the security flaws, which affect SonicWall GMS 9.5.2 and earlier versions, are below -

  • CVE-2026-109593 (CVSS score: 9.1) - An unauthenticated file read vulnerability that could allow an attacker with network access to read internal GMS files, potentially exposing sensitive information.
  • CVE-2026-109594 (CVSS score: 6.8) - A post-authentication SQL injection vulnerability that could allow an authenticated attacker to access or modify information stored in the GMS database under specific conditions.

"The affected product has reached End-of-life (EoL)," SonicWall said in a Tuesday alert.

"As a result, no remediation or security update will be released for these vulnerabilities. Organizations using the product should be aware of the associated security risks and are strongly encouraged to upgrade to the SonicWall Network Security Manager (NSM)."

The development comes less than a month after SonicWall shipped fixes for CVE-2026-102255 (CVSS score: 10.0), a critical pre-authenticated server-side request forgery (SSRF) flaw that could have allowed an attacker to reach internal functionality and perform unauthorized operations.

The vulnerability has since come under active exploitation in the wild, with telemetry data from Previdian recording 2,541 attack attempts from eight unique IP addresses from Singapore and the U.S. since October 9, 2026. As many as 30 exploitation attempts were registered on November 3, 2026.

content:
The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has added a security flaw in WordPress Core to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, citing evidence of active exploitation.

The high-severity vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-119977 (CVSS score: 8.1), is a case of Time-of-check Time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition that could be exploited to achieve arbitrary code execution on affected servers. Patches for the flaw were released late last month.

"WordPress Core contains a time-of-check time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition vulnerability that could allow unauthenticated attackers to execute code on the server during the upgrade window," CISA said. "This is due to predictable, web-accessible staging paths used during full-package core upgrades."

Details of the flaw emerged last week when Wordfence said exploiting the vulnerability does not require an account on the site. That said, it does require an attacker to exploit a brief window during a complete Core update that could allow unauthenticated code execution.

During the first 21 hours after public disclosure, the WordPress security company said it recorded more than 18,500 requests targeting staged "setup-config.php" installer paths. As of writing, 12,632 attacks attempting to exploit the flaw have been blocked in the last 24 hours.

Telemetry data from Previdian shows that three exploitation attempts have been recorded against its honeypot censors from an IP address geolocated in the U.K. The exploitation events were observed on October 30, 2026.

With exploitation now officially confirmed by CISA, Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies have time until November 6, 2026, to apply the fixes.
