In Belgium, attackers switched cooling units into defrost mode, Stephan Moelans, chief executive of the refrigeration contractor Sabcobel,  told Belgi...
content:
Attackers remotely changed the settings on refrigeration controls at supermarkets in Belgium, Sweden, Estonia and other European countries overnight into Monday, November 2, warming fridges and freezers.

No chain reported more than several dozen affected stores, and some had to throw away chilled and frozen food or take it off the shelf. Danfoss, a Danish maker of refrigeration controls, said its products were involved, as they were three weeks earlier when attackers hit hundreds of French supermarkets.

No one had claimed the attacks by Monday night, and it was not known whether they were linked to the attack in France.

Refrigeration controls are computers that run a store's fridges and freezers. They can be connected to the internet, allowing refrigeration contractors to monitor them and fix faults remotely.

In Belgium, attackers switched cooling units into defrost mode, Stephan Moelans, chief executive of the refrigeration contractor Sabcobel, told Belgian media. Defrost mode is meant to clear ice, but in these attacks it made the units heat up instead of keeping food cold. Sabcobel manages refrigeration systems for the Delhaize supermarket chain.

In other cases, the temperature setting was raised. An ICA store in Sjöbo, in southern Sweden, said its fridges and freezers had been set to 50°C and that staff were throwing out the affected goods.

At a Selver supermarket in Estonia, a freezer was set to 50°C, said Jann Mutso, chief executive of the refrigeration supplier Kitman Coldtech. Its temperature rose by only about 2-3°C, and the problem was resolved within about 10 minutes, with no products damaged.

Danfoss's security advisories page listed no advisory about the attacks when The Hacker News checked on November 3. The most detailed steps for operators are still those in an October alert from CERT-FR, part of France's national cybersecurity agency.

Which Companies Say They Were Hit

Each company described the incident in its own words, and not all of them called it a cyberattack.

Country Company Stores affected What the company or its supplier said
Belgium, Luxembourg Delhaize Several dozen, mostly in Belgium and a few in Luxembourg An "IT incident" affected refrigeration. The range of fresh and frozen food was temporarily limited.
Belgium Carrefour 15 of more than 700 A cyberattack on its refrigeration, with very limited impact.
Belgium Intermarché 10 to 15 Problems with its fridges.
Belgium Spar, under Colruyt Group 5, run by independent owners Their fridge systems were attacked.
Belgium IKEA 1, in Mons A cyber incident hit the store's fridges and freezers. No other IKEA store in Belgium was affected.
Sweden ICA A limited number. No count given An incident affected refrigeration and freezer systems. ICA did not confirm a cyberattack.
Sweden Coop 6 (to TT and AFP) or 7 (to Reuters and Bloomberg), of about 800 A cyber incident in which someone tampered with its refrigeration without permission.
Ireland Musgrave, owner of SuperValu 13 of 223 A "cyber incident" limited to one refrigeration model.
Estonia Selver, through supplier Kitman Coldtech 1 An attack on an older Danfoss system.
Netherlands Businesses not named At least 17 businesses, including butchers and small local shops Attacked, according to Danfoss.
Finland Kesko A few smaller stores Unusual temperatures. The cause was under investigation. The stores' equipment is outside Kesko's central protections.
Portugal Intermarché, Mosqueteiros group 7 A cyberattack that appears to have targeted an outside company managing the refrigeration, according to AFP.
Italy Coop supermarkets run by Radenza Group At least 4, in Sicily An attack on its remote control system for frozen food sections, according to AFP.

At a De Laet & Van Haver butcher shop in Hove, south of Antwerp, the fridges were turned up as high as 18°C, owner Luc De Laet told Reuters. He estimated that about €15,000 worth of meat was ruined.

At the 13 SuperValu stores, Musgrave took chilled and frozen products off sale as a precaution. The company said on Monday afternoon that the incident had been resolved and restocking was under way.

What Companies Say About the Equipment and the Way In

Several of the systems that were hit were made by Danfoss. All of ICA's affected stores were connected to an outside refrigeration control system supplied by Danfoss, an ICA spokesperson told AFP. In Estonia, attackers reached the control computer of an older Danfoss system, Mutso said.

Danfoss is not named in every case. Musgrave's statement did not name the maker of the affected model.

An affected Belgian butcher told Dutch broadcaster NOS that equipment from a second maker, Copeland, was also attacked in Belgium. Copeland gave NOS no clear answer to questions about the attacks.

The Dutch systems that were hit were not on a secure network and still used default passwords, a Danfoss spokesperson told NOS. Most shops there had taken measures after the French attack, but a few had not, and those were the ones hit.

Danfoss also told Belgian broadcaster VTM that the weakness lies mainly in outdated software and that customers who had not updated were affected, Euronews reported.

Sabcobel knows of about 20 affected units among the hundreds it manages in Belgium. In the Belgian cases, attackers got into individual supermarkets' systems, not those of refrigeration contractors, Moelans told Belgian media. Sabcobel had advised stores to secure their internet connections, and many but not all had done so.

Mutso said old controllers that had not been updated were being targeted. Selver said the store that was hit was the last one it had not yet moved to a new system. ICA told NBC News that its own systems were not affected and that the affected stores used an outside supplier and were connected to a network outside ICA's central network.

Belgium's Centre for Cybersecurity told reporters on Monday that it had no further information. Sweden's National Cybersecurity Centre did not say in its notice how attackers got in.

What Operators Can Do

CERT-FR's alert covers Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC series controllers, as well as Copeland xweb and Dixell xweb. It says attack campaigns against these devices are probably still underway. When The Hacker News checked on November 3, the alert had last been updated on October 16.

For devices that have not been compromised, the steps are:

  1. Make sure the devices cannot be reached from the internet, including any device on a public IP address. Check your insurance contract before cutting the data feed to your refrigeration contractor.
  2. Check the whole configuration, especially the defrost schedules.
  3. Restore access only through a secure VPN or a protected network. In an emergency, you can filter the contractors' IP addresses at a firewall, but this should not be a lasting fix.
  4. Follow the maker's good practices, such as updating firmware. For Danfoss devices, set the security level to Strict and make sure default passwords have been changed.

For a device that has been compromised, two more steps follow: restart the Danfoss device or reset it to factory settings, then reconfigure it before putting it back into service.

End-of-life devices that no longer get security fixes are very likely to be compromised if they stay on the internet, CERT-FR warns. A factory reset alone leaves them open to attack again. In October, Danfoss said most of the units hit in France were older models it no longer updates, the AK-SM 800 and AK-SC 355.

Danfoss advised Dutch customers on October 13 to disconnect their systems from the internet and reconnect them only through a secure network. It had also been working with customers to put fixes in place.

Sweden's National Cybersecurity Center advised organizations to list which devices are connected to the internet, decide whether each one needs to be connected, and keep any that remain connected updated and protected with multiple layers of security.

Moelans said a software update alone is not enough, because the installations need physical changes that cost money. The simplest answer is a secure internet connection for managing the fridges, which most of Sabcobel's customers adopted after the French attack.

Who Is Behind It

Danfoss said the Dutch attacks were the same kind as the one in France, Sabcobel said the same method was used in Belgium, and Kitman said the method in Estonia was similar. A shared method does not show that the same people carried out both attacks.

Belgium's Centre for Cybersecurity said on Monday that it was not known who was behind the attacks and that "it may never be determined".

Belgium's federal prosecutor's office has opened a criminal investigation, it confirmed to VRT. Sweden's National Cybersecurity Centre said on Monday that it was following the incidents and sharing information with agencies in other Nordic and European countries.

title: cPGuard Update Channel Hijacked to Backdoor Linux Servers and Collect Password Hashes
author: The Hacker News
summary: An attacker broke into the update system of the cPGuard security tool on November 2 and used it to send a malicious script to customers' Linux servers.   The script installed a backdoor and collected password hashes and other sensitive files from servers that ran it, cPGuard maker OPSSHIELD said in an advisory . The attack was detected within 12 hours of those versions going out, according to OPSSHIELD. The company has cleared its infrastructure credentials and stopped the script from reaching more servers. content:
An attacker broke into the update system of the cPGuard security tool on November 2 and used it to send a malicious script to customers' Linux servers.

The script installed a backdoor and collected password hashes and other sensitive files from servers that ran it, cPGuard maker OPSSHIELD said in an advisory. The attacker has since taken some of that data.

cPGuard 5.88.25 and later versions remove the backdoor and the files the script left. Credentials the script copied may still work after the update, so any server that may have run the script also needs new passwords and keys.

At 02:06 UTC, the attacker, who has not been identified, used compromised credentials to get into cPGuard's update system. The script went out in cPGuard versions 5.88.12 through 5.88.19.

The attack was detected within 12 hours of those versions going out, according to OPSSHIELD. The company has cleared its infrastructure credentials and stopped the script from reaching more servers. It is still investigating how the attacker got the credentials.

OPSSHIELD has not said how many servers installed one of these versions. Servers check for updates at intervals, so some may not have run the script.

Admins can check whether a server installed an affected version by searching its update log:

grep 'Successfully updated' /opt/cpguard/logs/install_log

An entry for any version from 5.88.12 through 5.88.19 means the server installed an affected update. The entry alone does not show that the script ran or that data left the server. The server should still be treated as potentially compromised, even if it now runs 5.88.25 or later.

A server with no matching entries, or with a missing or incomplete log, may still have run the script. Admins who are unsure can contact OPSSHIELD Support.

The script collected these kinds of data, OPSSHIELD found: /etc/shadow and /etc/passwd, root's MariaDB or MySQL configuration (my.cnf), root's shell history, and the SSH authorization and known-hosts files for root. It may not have collected every file from every server, and the company is still working out what left each one.

The /etc/shadow file stores one-way password hashes. Weak, common or previously leaked passwords can be recovered from those hashes by testing guesses offline, and even strong ones still need resetting. Secrets that may sit in the database configuration or shell history have no such hashing to protect them.

The script uploaded what it collected to a licensing server run by OPSSHIELD itself, using a compromised account, so the attacker could pick it up later. OPSSHIELD has since secured that account.

The attacker took 32 files from that server, each tied to one customer server, OPSSHIELD estimated late on November 2 UTC. The count covers only files known to have been taken, and it may change. It does not show how many servers may be involved in total.

Beyond the data collection and the backdoor, OPSSHIELD has found no other malicious activity so far, a finding it says is not final.

What cPGuard Admins Should Do Now

OPSSHIELD asks admins to update every cPGuard server now and confirm the version:

  1. Run cpgcli update --start on each server.
  2. Run cpgcli --version and check that it reports 5.88.25 or later. If the update fails or the version is lower, contact OPSSHIELD Support.

Admins should also take these steps for any server where the script ran or may have run:

  1. From a trusted recovery environment, reset the passwords for root and every other local Linux account that uses a password.
  2. From a trusted device, change any of those passwords that are also used on other systems.
  3. Rotate the server's database passwords, S3 access keys, DigitalOcean tokens and any secrets recorded in root's shell history.
  4. Replace the SSH private keys stored under /root/.ssh, and remove the matching old public keys from every system that trusts them.

OPSSHIELD is not recommending a full reset or operating system rebuild as a routine step, and says that view could change as the investigation continues. Admins who find other signs of compromise, or cannot confirm a server is clean, should ask OPSSHIELD Support for a case-by-case review, which may lead to a rebuild.

Separately, OPSSHIELD is releasing another update, as a precaution, that removes its support-access keys from cPGuard servers where they were added earlier.

Support access is a cPGuard feature customers use to let OPSSHIELD staff into a server for troubleshooting. Granting it adds an SSH public key belonging to OPSSHIELD to the authorized_keys file for root, according to the company's documentation.

OPSSHIELD has not said whether the private key that matches its support-access key was exposed in the attack.

Files the Script Left Behind

OPSSHIELD published these file names. The update removes the backdoor shell and the collection directory, so their absence after updating proves nothing about whether the script ran.

  • File: cpguard-v58812-i91511.sh (the malicious script)
  • File: /var/tmp/.cpg91511_sh (backdoor shell)
  • Directory: /var/tmp/.cpg91511 (where the script gathered files)
  • File: /var/tmp/.cpg91511/loot.tgz (archive the script prepared)

title: Attackers Exploit Critical Siemens IoT2050 Flaw to Plant Remote Command Backdoors
author: The Hacker News
summary: A maximum-severity security flaw impacting Siemens SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced devices has come under active exploitation, VulnCheck has revealed .   The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-58115 (CVSS score: 10.0), is a case of missing authentication for a critical function that could be exploited by an unauthenticated remote attacker to run arbitrary code. The issue has been remediated in versions 4.3.4.1 or later. As mitigations, Siemens recommends  that users uninstall Node-RED or harden the installation by following the steps below -      Enabling HTTPS access    Securing the editor and admin API via cre...
content:
A maximum-severity security flaw impacting Siemens SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced devices has come under active exploitation, VulnCheck has revealed.

The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-58115 (CVSS score: 10.0), is a case of missing authentication for a critical function that could be exploited by an unauthenticated remote attacker to run arbitrary code.

"SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced devices running Industrial OS with Node-RED installed contain a missing authentication vulnerability in the Node-RED HTTP interface that could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to create malicious flows and execute arbitrary code on the underlying server with maximum privileges," Siemens said in an advisory released back in August 2026.

The issue has been remediated in versions 4.3.4.1 or later. As mitigations, Siemens recommends that users uninstall Node-RED or harden the installation by following the steps below -

  • Enabling HTTPS access
  • Securing the editor and admin API via credential based authentication or through an OAuth/OpenID provider
  • Securing the HTTP Nodes and Node-RED Dashboard using basic authentication

As of October 30, 2026, VulnCheck said it observed attackers attempting to weaponize CVE-2026-58115 against its honeypot network in an attempt to download and run a Linux bot.

"The attacker's request was a complete exploit," VulnCheck researcher Patrick Garrity said. "It deployed a Node-RED flow, triggered it automatically, and pulled a binary from an attacker-controlled server, all behind three layers of encoding."

Specifically, the malicious flow is designed to run a shell script wrapper, which uses wget to retrieve the botnet binary for AMD64 architecture from 85.215.73[.]250. Curl is used as a fallback if the wget attempt fails. In the final stage, the binary is saved as "/dev/shm/.b" and executed.

Since then, the attackers behind the campaign have switched to a two-stage process where the wget command is used to retrieve another shell script ("wget.sh") from the same server.

Another request has been found to run wget/curl against "45.194.90[.]57:38472" to fetch a payload called ".sys_update," save it on disk as "/tmp/.kworker" in an attempt to disguise it as a harmless kernel worker thread," and then execute it. The exact functionality of "wget.sh" or ".kworker" remains unknown, as they could not be retrieved.

"Several requests deployed no downloader at all. Instead, the flow exposes an HTTP in endpoint (for example /cmd, or a randomly named path) wired through a function node to an exec node with addpay enabled, so the attacker could run arbitrary commands later by passing them in a query parameter," Garrity said. "This backdoor survives even if a memory-backed implant is lost on reboot."

title: Attackers Target Unpatched CryptoPayment Gateway Flaw That Can Expose Wallet Credentials
author: The Hacker News

The vulnerability in question is CVE-2026-81648, which carries a CVSS score of 10.0. content:
Threat actors are attempting to exploit an unpatched maximum-severity security vulnerability in the CryptoPayment Gateway WordPress plugin, according to findings from Defused Cyber.

The vulnerability in question is CVE-2026-81648, which carries a CVSS score of 10.0. Successful exploitation of the flaw could permit unauthenticated users to delete arbitrary files on the server and extract sensitive data, including stored wallet credentials.

"The CryptoPayment Gateway WordPress plugin from 1.2.1 to 1.2.2 does not apply an authorization check on one of its AJAX endpoints, allowing unauthenticated users to invoke administrative operations, including deleting arbitrary files on the server, overwriting the payment gateway configuration and recovering stored wallet credentials in cleartext," according to a description of the flaw on the NIST National Vulnerability Database (NVD).

The vulnerability affects versions 1.2.1 through 1.2.2, which is the latest version. There are no known fixes for the flaw, according to WP Scan. As of August 28, 2026, the plugin has been closed on the WordPress Plugin Directory and is no longer available for download due to an unspecified "security issue."

Statistics show that the plugin has been collectively downloaded 1,845 times, including 20 downloads over the last seven days. It's unclear if it's actively installed on any WordPress sites.

"We are observing in-the-wild exploitation attempts against CVE-2026-81648, a critical (CVSS 10.0) flaw in the CryptoPayment Gateway for WordPress," Defused Cyber said in an X post. "The attacks we recorded came from infrastructure that markets themselves as 'Anonymous KYC-Free VPS Hosting.'"

In the absence of a fix, site owners are advised to remove the plugin, rotate wallet keys, and audit for any suspicious changes.

title: Microsoft once tried to buy Nintendo and got laughed out of the room, now...
author: Abhijith M B
summary: Microsoft first asked Nintendo to be acquired, then offered to build its consoles in January 2000. Both failed, and Square and Midway said no too. Microsoft bought Bungie instead, and Halo made the Xb...
content:
Before the original Xbox launched in 2001, Microsoft asked Nintendo if it would consider being acquired, and according to a former Xbox executive, Nintendo “just laughed their asses off.” Microsoft then went back with a second pitch in January 2000, offering to build Nintendo’s hardware while Nintendo focused on Mario and its games. It didn’t work out either.

With the Xbox turning 25 on November 15, the tables have turned quite literally. Nintendo is selling Switch 2 consoles by the millions, while XBOX’s CEO recently had to clarify that Xbox is not for sale.

Microsoft went to Nintendo twice before the first Xbox launched

When Microsoft was building the Xbox, it had money but no games, so the team tried to buy studios for exclusives. “The first company we reached out to buy was EA. They said, ‘No, thanks,’ and then Nintendo,” said Bob McBreen, then head of business development.

Kevin Bachus, then director of third-party relations, remembers how that went. “Steve [Ballmer] made us go meet with Nintendo to see if they would consider being acquired. They just laughed their asses off. Like, imagine an hour of somebody just laughing at you.” I always wondered if high-stakes corporate meetings were just as how it is portrayed in movies, and now I have my answer.

Undeterred, Microsoft tried a different approach. “We actually had Nintendo in our building in January 2000 to work through the details of a joint venture where we gave them all the technical specs of the Xbox,” McBreen said, adding that “the pitch was their hardware stunk,” and Nintendo would let Microsoft “take care of the hardware.” It didn’t work out.

Ballmer’s only comment was, “I remember loving their content.” Nintendo of America’s then-chairman Howard Lincoln was more diplomatic, saying, “Nintendo does not talk about confidential discussions with other companies. In any event, nothing came of these discussions.”

These recollections come from Bloomberg’s oral history of the Xbox by Dina Bass, published in January 2021.

Sony’s PlayStation 2 scared Microsoft into making a console

In 1999, Sony announced the PlayStation 2 and marketed it as a rival to the PC. “Sony coming out and saying, ‘PlayStation 2 is going to redefine the computer world,’ that got attention inside of Microsoft,” said Bachus.

Rick Thompson, the first head of Xbox, said Sony was showing “a home without a PC in it,” and “You can’t say that to Steve Ballmer.” Well, Ballmer’s words are iconic: “We needed to penetrate the living room.”

The PS2 launched in Japan on March 4, 2000, and doubled as a DVD player. Nintendo, meanwhile, was still on the cartridge-based Nintendo 64 while working on its next console, codenamed Dolphin. But Nintendo wasn’t struggling; in fact, it was the opposite. Pokémon was a global craze, the Game Boy Color was everywhere, and Mario and Zelda were what Microsoft didn’t have in their portfolio.

Microsoft couldn’t buy Nintendo, so it bought Halo

Nintendo wasn’t the only one that got away. Microsoft had a letter of intent to buy Square, the Final Fantasy publisher, until its banker said in November 1999 that “the price is too low.” Talks with Mortal Kombat maker Midway also fizzled out.

Then came Bungie, whose unreleased Halo Steve Jobs had shown off at Macworld 1999. Microsoft bought it in 2000, and Midway’s CEO left Bachus a voicemail calling Microsoft “the dumbest people in the industry” for buying a PC game developer. Even Microsoft Japan believed first-person shooters don’t do well on consoles.

Halo: Combat Evolved launched with the Xbox on November 15, 2001, three days before Nintendo’s GameCube reached North America, and it became the console’s runaway hit. As Bachus said, “Halo was why you, as an Xbox owner, were smarter than your PlayStation 2-owning friends.”

Anyway, the company that got laughed out of Nintendo’s meeting went on to buy Bethesda and, in 2023, Activision Blizzard for $69 billion.

Nintendo and XBOX took very different paths

Today, Nintendo is doing just fine. Maybe, more than fine. As of June 30, 2026, the original Switch had sold 156.59 million units, and the Switch 2 has already crossed 23.68 million.

XBOX, now in all caps after Asha Sharma ran a fan poll in May, is in a reset. Its revenue fell 7% to $21.79 billion in fiscal 2026, with hardware revenue down 29%, and Microsoft is cutting 3,200 XBOX roles. In September, Sharma told The New York Times that “Xbox is not for sale” amid reports of a possible spin-off.

Funnily enough, Mario didn’t make it to Xbox, but Microsoft now publishes its own games on Nintendo’s consoles, with Minecraft on Switch for years. XBOX is also going full swing on Windows, with Xbox mode on Windows 11 PCs and a next-gen console that could push Windows 11 performance forward.

For the 25th anniversary, Microsoft is releasing the XBOX Series X25 in translucent green, a nod to the original console. I can’t help but wonder what that anniversary would have looked like with Mario on the box. What do you think? Would Nintendo have survived as part of Microsoft?

title: October was Xbox's biggest months for new games, with 210 titles vying for wallets
author: Alexander Cope
summary: KoreaXboxNews showed that 210 Xbox games were released in October 2026, 95 of which had Xbox Play Anywhere, as debate around market saturation grows.
content:
October 2026 was an extremely stacked month for Xbox games, with titles like Gears of War: E-Day, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, Final Fantasy Resonance, and many vying for attention and our wallets.

How many games, you ask? Well, via analysis from @KoreaXBOXnews on X, 210 Xbox games launched in October 2026, 95 of which supported Xbox Play Anywhere.

That huge statistic highlights the general market challenge so far, as users debate market saturation. Gears of War: E-Day and its virtue as an "exclusive" game on Xbox has been under a microscope, with claims that the game hasn't delivered for Microsoft. Even if that was true, it was among many big high-quality releases actively competing with hundreds of other Xbox games at once for attention, and that's without mentioning the 187 Xbox games released in September 2026.

Latest Videos FromWindows Central

On the plus side, @KoreaXBOXnews's analysis shows that Xbox Play Anywhere is gaining more momentum, consistently hovering around 50% share since June 2026 (or 70% if you count "triple-stack" achievement games, otherwise known as shovelware titles. Microsoft is cracking down on this exploitative practice, where developers ship multiple versions of the same game to bait achievement hunters.)

This means Microsoft is focusing on encouraging more games adopt Xbox Play Anywhere going forward, as more people are liking the idea of buying an Xbox game once and then being able to play it on console, handheld, and Windows PC within the Xbox ecosystem.

Can't say I blame them because being able to buy and play a game on an Xbox Series X|S, and then being able to play on an Xbox Ally X while carrying over data with no extra charge is a pretty good deal.

title: Former Xbox COO Helen Chiang denies violating policies in parting LinkedIn post
author: Jez Corden
summary: Microsoft's former Xbox COO Helen Chiang had some words about her firing on LinkedIn earlier today, titled "Clarity is Kindness," in an apparent shot at Xbox CEO Asha Sharma.
content:
Microsoft's COO Helen Chiang was fired from Xbox a few weeks ago, after 27 years of top-level leadership spent across the org, most prolifically at Minecraft.

The removal was abrupt and somewhat confusing on the face of it. Chiang was widely respected across the Microsoft stack and is a trusted figure, described to me as "by the book" by our own sources. When it emerged that she had been fired for "policy violations," it added an unexpected twist that left us with more questions than answers, ultimately.

Now, Helen Chiang has responded to the incident on LinkedIn, titled "Clarity is Kindness," which is a comment Xbox CEO Asha Sharma made to the WSJ while discussing the health of Microsoft's gaming business recently.

There has been some speculation about my abrupt departure from Microsoft, including claims that I was “fired for a policy violation”. That’s not accurate," Chiang writes, "silence should not be mistaken for agreement. What has been said about my departure, and what has been left unsaid, has created a picture of me that I hardly recognize. It’s important to me to set the record straight."

In the full post shared below, Chiang denies that she leaked information, sought employment at Microsoft competitors, engaged in insider trading, bullying, or embezzlement, or that she left because she didn't get the CEO job. She says that she always hoped to stay at Microsoft and "keep building," and this departure wasn't what she envisioned.

"I share this because I don’t want my departure reduced to an inaccurate story about incompetence, ambition for the next big job, or a Nelson-level scandal."

As to not paraphrase, I've included the full text from the post below.

"Clarity is Kindness

There has been some speculation about my abrupt departure from Microsoft, including claims that I was “fired for a policy violation”. That’s not accurate and while I won’t turn this into a play-by-play, silence should not be mistaken for agreement. What has been said about my departure, and what has been left unsaid, has created a picture of me that I hardly recognize. It’s important to me to set the record straight.

First, I did not leak confidential company information to the press. I have never communicated with any journalist outside the limited, company-authorized interviews I’ve done as part of my job. That includes every journalist who reached out this week seeking my side of the story.

Second, I did not leave XBOX to join a competitor. You don’t spend two decades somewhere without developing a deep loyalty to the people, teams, and businesses you’ve helped build. XBOX was never just another stop in my career. My end game was always to keep building here.

Third, I did not engage in discrimination, bullying, harassment, insider trading, embezzlement, or other fraudulent activity. I stand by my record: both the results I delivered and the way I have treated people throughout my career. I won’t let speculation define my character or erase that record.

Lastly, I did not leave because I was passed over for a bigger role. Since having children, I’ve been intentional about how I define ambition and success. I haven’t actively sought out bigger roles or increased responsibilities, and the last time I interviewed for a job was in 2011. My reputation and results paved the way for the opportunities that followed. I went where the company believed I was needed and where I could have the greatest impact. I did not ask for my most recent role, either. I was promoted into it in July.

I believe in fairness, accountability, and holding ourselves to the standards we expect of others. Those standards only mean something when they’re applied consistently. I have serious concerns about how they were applied in my case, and I believe those concerns deserve to be taken seriously.

I share this because I don’t want my departure reduced to an inaccurate story about incompetence, ambition for the next big job, or a Nelson-level scandal. My story is about staying true to your core values, especially when it is hard. That’s the legacy I hope to leave behind.

To everyone who has reached out with hugs, love, and support: thank you. So many of you have reminded me of the wonderful times we’ve shared over the past 20 years and the impact we’ve had on one another. Some of you I haven’t been in touch with for several years, yet you still took the time to check on me. Others are people I’ve never even met, but you reached out anyway. That speaks volumes about the care and humanity in our industry and the connections that transcend where we work.

This is not how I ever imagined my story here would end. And it is not the whole story." — Helen Chiang, former Xbox COO.

Helen Chiang's somewhat unceremonious departure comes amidst widespread upheaval at Xbox as Microsoft restructures its gaming org, which has led to thousands of layoffs, divestitures, and studio closures. Microsoft managed to return some studios to independent ownership and has sold others to publishers, as it tries to rein in spending in general.

The Coalition has been put on the hook for $500 million per Microsoft's finance auditors, who only see the dollars and not the complexity of game development, the impact the pandemic had on the development of games between Gears 5 and E-Day, and other mitigating factors.

Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has returned the brand's focus to its core customers in recent months, with a return of exclusive games, boosting investment in the existing console infrastructure, and improving things on the back end for game developers.

I suspect there'll be more disruption before things calm down ... as the industry in general reels from an overabundance of content, reduced consumer spending, and the AI-fostered RAMpocalypse.

title: Here's what's new for Warzone when it integrates with Modern Warfare 4
author: Richard Devine
summary: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Season 1 goes live on November 6, and it's bringing Warzone into the mix for the first time. Here's what we know about how things will look.
content:
The integration of Call of Duty: Warzone with Modern Warfare 4 is happening on November 6 when Season 1 begins for this year's game.

While it also means the end of Warzone for players on Xbox One and PS4, it will be bringing a bunch of new content to the table. When the switchover happens, there will be two brand-new maps to play at first, alongside two returning classic maps at some point later in the season.

Besides access to all the new weapons from Modern Warfare 4, the battle pass, the leveling and prestige system, Camo challenges, and Calling Cards, there are also some quality-of-life improvements, too. Here's a brief overview of what's coming.

Two new Call of Duty: Warzone maps: Hajin and Zodiac

At the launch of Season 1 there will be two Warzone maps to play, and they're both brand-new for the Modern Warfare 4 year: Hajin and Zodiac.

Zodiac we've already seen during the Modern Warfare 4 beta period earlier this year. Set around a drone manufacturing facility in South Korea, Zodiac is the new Resurgence map and will be joined in the rotation by the returning Rebirth Island at some point during the season.

You may like
  • Warzone players will have to wait to find out more about the integration with MW4
  • When is Warzone merging with Modern Warfare 4?
  • We've finally got some actual details on Modern Warfare 4's DMZ mode

Hajin is the new "big map" for Battle Royale. Set across North and South Korea, anyone who's already jumped in to play DMZ will be familiar with the Hajin location. It appears to be the same physical map, so those players will already have a leg up on the terrain.

It's been a pretty good location for DMZ so far, and while there are areas with tall buildings, there are also plenty that are more open, and the terrain is quite varied. Also coming across from DMZ is the variable weather, so one match it might be sunny and clear, and another the map may be shrouded in fog. Hajin will also have two new Gulags.

The previous big map, Verdansk, will be joining the Battle Royale rotation at some point during the season, bringing some new POIs along with it.

New features and weapons for Warzone under Modern Warfare 4

Besides the new map, there are also some new features and just overall quality-of-life improvements for Warzone beginning with Season 1. These include:

  • Tactical Sprint will be available to all Operators without the need for a Perk, but its duration is slightly shortened.
  • Players can drag their allies while reviving them, pulling them out of harm’s way.
  • Additional weapon balance tuning.
  • Improved visibility and readability across all maps.
  • Improved footstep audio

Tactical Sprint is probably a big one for Warzone players, and while it doesn't sound like it will be overpowered, it will at least help in keeping that fast-flowing experience players have become familiar with.

What to read next
  • What you need to know about Call of Duty: Warzone shutting down on Xbox One
  • Explaining what carries forward into Modern Warfare 4 from Black Ops 7
  • Modern Warfare 4 DMZ will be getting a new map in Season 1

Without it applied in multiplayer in Modern Warfare 4, you can feel quite slow, and that was never going to work in Warzone.

It'll be interesting to see what the weapon balancing looks like, though. Additionally, the time to kill (TTK). In DMZ, PvP encounters are often over before you even spot who's firing at you, so hopefully Warzone has found a balance here. There are definitely some weapons that already feel like everyone will gravitate towards them, but it'd be nice if there's a wider meta than there often is.

All of the weapons from Modern Warfare 4 and the new ones introduced in Season 1 will be available to Warzone players, as will their attachments, including Apex.

Legacy weapons from as far back as Modern Warfare 2 will remain accessible in Warzone. These will be available as a five-attachment version, alongside any previously acquired legacy weapon blueprints.

Additionally, and what sounds quite interesting to me, is that on Hajin, Zodiac, and Verdansk, we'll now have movable interactive objects. These include fuel barrels, which will go boom, and apparently objects such as dumpsters and "pyramids" that can be used to create cover. Or roadblocks. So maybe keep an extra eye out when you're driving.

Players will also be able to get their hands on Elite Perks, which will add a fourth perk to their loadout. These are found in-match at Buy Stations, and more can be obtained through Supply Run contracts. But only one can be active at a time.

Oh, and the Aston Martin Dreadnought vehicle that we've been driving about in DMZ will also be joining Warzone.

Call of Duty: Warzone Season 1 game modes

Camo grinders will be delighted to hear that casual mode has returned for both Battle Royale and Resurgence and will be available on all maps.

Additionally, at Season 1 launch there will be three limited-time modes (LTMs):

  • Rally Point LTM
  • Loaded Resurgence
  • Massive Resurgence

Additional LTMs are promised throughout Season 1, including Rockets and Snipers, and Extreme Resurgence.

Rally Point is described as a casual mode designed to help new and returning players get to grips with the mechanics of Warzone, as well as check out the new Zodiac map and learn about some of the new features. 20 players will be in each lobby.

"Rally Point is a no-circle, infinite Resurgence, and Drop-In/Drop-Out mode, allowing players to come and go as they please."

For completing the challenges in this mode, there will be an exclusive weapon blueprint and two camos to unlock.

Loaded Resurgence will be across Zodiac and Rebirth Island and looks the same as we've known it before. Drop in with your preferred loadout and earn new perks with eliminations as you try to get to Specialist.

Massive Resurgence is Resurgence, but on the Hajin big map with 120 players. There aren't any special rewards listed for these modes right now, but that doesn't mean there won't be some.

Call of Duty: Warzone Mode Mastery camos arrive from Season 1

While much of the camo grind in Modern Warfare 4 is universal across multiplayer, DMZ, and now Warzone, like the others, there is a dedicated set of Mode Mastery challenges to complete. And now we know what we'll have to do.

  • Parallax: Get 5 kills in a match 300 times.
  • Damascus Reforged: Get 2 kills without plating 200 times.
  • Empyros: Place in the top 5 with at least 6 kills 75 times.

Presumably we'll still be able to do the Mode Mastery camos in casual mode, too, but even so, they're still going to be a pretty long process. The saving grace is that if you've been playing Modern Warfare 4, this year you at least already have a head start.

Nevertheless, I spent 65 hours doing last year's Warzone Mastery Camo, even using casual mode, and I feel like this year's is going to take longer than that. I'm not sure I have it in me. We'll see.

Additionally, there will be a "Return to Call of Duty: Warzone" event running with some additional camos to get your hands on. And who doesn't like some shiny camos?

Season 1 for both Modern Warfare 4 and Warzone goes live on November 6 at midnight ET (9pm Pacific) globally. Additionally, it will be available on the Nintendo Switch for the first time. Find the full details on the Warzone integration at the Call of Duty Blog.

title: Enlightenment desktop 0.28 released with better networking
author: OMG! Ubuntu!
content:
Enlightenment 0.28 has been released, the first major update to the open-source desktop environment since early 2025.

Given the time between this and the previous 0.27 release, the changelog is suitably lengthy. Networking and audio stack enhancements, UI and UX tweaks and, of course, plenty of bug fixes are listed – no jaw-dropping UI changes, though.

v0.28 adds a new Network Manager module. This supports connecting to and managing wireless, wired and Bluetooth networking connections, as well as VPNs. It plays signal strength, security and other connection details.

On the audio side, a native PipeWire mixer is available alongside the existing PulseAudio one, and mixer actions can now cycle between different ‘sinks’ and change between device outputs.

Copy and paste a lot? There’s an integrated clipboard history module keeping a semi-persistent log. It has options to control what content is tracked, for how long, lets you clear items and decide if contents should persist between sessions.

Enlightenment 0.28 also improves its support on portable devices, gaining support for enabling and configuring battery charge limits (to help preserve battery health), ACPI CPU power profiles (kernel-provided) and better polling of resources.

Fixes are numerous, looping in a grab-bag of window management buffs, better pointer handling and focus selection, monitor DDC and EDID detection and more. Per-desktop and per-screen profile support was removed, though.

Install Enlightenment 0.28 on Ubuntu

Enlightenment’s website has a link to download the source code of E28, which you can compile by hand, though Enlightenment 0.28.0 depends on EFL v1.29.0 or newer, so you’ll need to download and build that too.

Don’t need the latest changes? Ubuntu 26.04 has an older version of Enlightenment in the archives you can install with apt.

Don’t fancy building it from source? Depending on which version of Ubuntu you use, there are scripts that automate the entire process:

  • For Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, use eeminent
  • For Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, run equivoke
  • For Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, opt for elluminate

Don’t expect something as flashy or as fluid as GNOME or KDE.

Enlightenment (aka as ‘E’) is a modular desktop, with its window manager, compositor and core desktop shell built using Enlightenment Foundation Libraries (EFL). It offers a set of native EFL-based apps, including file manager, photo viewer and terminal.

The “aesthetic” has never been for everyone, nor its overall user experience (being modular can feel jarring). But as it is incredibly lightweight and configurable, without being basic, it’s worth playing around with on a rainy day.

title: Convincing footage of a Persona 1 remake for Xbox may have just leaked
author: Alexander Cope
summary: Over the past couple of days, players have been ecstatic over a new YouTube video that appears to be a 'leaked' gameplay trailer for what appears to be a remake of the first game in Atlus' Persona ser...
content:
Over the weekend, YouTuber "P1REMAKE" uploaded a new video that has every Persona fan up in arms with excitement and speculation — a supposed gameplay trailer for a Persona 1 Remake that's coming to Xbox.

The video contains a gameplay montage of characters exploring a school filled with monsters, a visual-novel-style cutscene, and turn-based combat similar to that of modern Persona games like Persona 3: Reload, Persona 4: Revival, and Persona 5: Royal.

The video also shows that it's coming to Xbox (and/or PC) because the UI display during combat shows Xbox controller face buttons (Y, X, B, A) and an RB shoulder button.

Now it's very likely that this video could be a fake trailer made by fans, especially since Atlus hasn't been motivated to take this video offline yet.

Then again, this video, despite its low resolution, looks too well put together to be fake or AI-generated. Plus, Atlus did express a desire to remake Persona 1 and 2 last summer. So, there is a chance this trailer could, in fact, be real or, at the very least, a fan-made or leaked proof of concept of what a Persona 1 remake could look like.

Either way, it'd be cool to see remakes of Persona 1 and 2 finally happen, as they are vastly different and darker in terms of tone, story, and gameplay style compared to their more popular successors.

We'll have to wait and see if Atlus indeed plans to remake the games that kick-started its flagship franchise at either the upcoming Game Awards or at a future Xbox Games Showcase, since that's where they tend to reveal Persona games these days.

In the meantime, we'll have Persona 4: Revival (releasing on February 18, 2027, for consoles and PC) and Persona 6 to look forward to.

title: Microsoft used AI to help build Windows 11's new speed test
author: Sean Endicott
summary: Microsoft's upcoming Windows 11 speed test tool is also an early example of how the company wants to use AI during development.
content:
Windows 11 has a new speed test feature in the works that will allow you to check your PC's connectivity without having to open a browser or a separate app. The feature is already in testing with Windows Insiders and looks promising so far.

Windows 11 already has a shortcut for testing internet speed, but it's simply a button that opens Bing's speed test in a web browser. The new speed test feature is built-in, making it feel like part of Windows 11 rather than a tacked-on browser shortcut.

The addition has been well-received and sparked positive discussions online. Our Mauro Huculak said, "Windows 11 needs more features like this," and his wish may come true.

Latest Videos FromWindows Central

Marcus Ash, lead of Design and Research across Windows & Devices, discussed the new speed test feature and how the tool was created. According to Ash, the new speed test feature is the result of an agentic AI workflow guided by a real person.

"This is where I see a lot of potential in AI," said Ash. "Using agentic workflows and WinUI 3 to build more integrated Windows experiences. Getting from idea to customer value faster. Without AI slop. That is the way."

You may like
  • Microsoft will finally replace Bing shortcut posing as a Windows 11 speed test
  • I wanted Windows 11 to stop opening Bing for a speed test, and Microsoft is fixing it
  • Windows 11's design boss admits it needs work, while AI fixes OS inconsistencies

AI is under heavy scrutiny for a variety of reasons. Many criticize "vibe coding," which often results in low-quality projects. But there is a place for AI in certain workflows.

After looking at Ash's comment, it's easy to see why Microsoft chose to attach the term "Copilot" to many of its AI products. The company's leaders view AI as a tool that works alongside people to streamline workflows while still leaning on the guidance of human expertise.

Considering the positive reception of the new speed test tool, it seems likely that other parts of Windows 11 will be built with a similar workflow. I'm curious to see if they will all be well-received or if some people will push back solely due to the use of AI.

What do you think about Microsoft using AI as part of its development process? Let us know in the comments!

title: Microsoft’s design boss fires back at Windows 11 critics over a missing Windows 10...
author: Abhijith M B
summary: Baca explains why an unlock step could add friction and interfere with taskbar icons and the system tray, reveals Windows 10 saw a significant volume of accidental taskbar moves, and says nothing is b...
content:
Microsoft’s Vice President of Design for Windows, Diego Baca, says a taskbar lock switch (like the one we had in Windows 10) won’t fix dragging the Windows 11 taskbar, as it adds an extra step and could interfere with rearranging taskbar icons or system tray items. He also pushed back on reports that said drag-to-move is never coming back to Windows 11, saying “Nothing is beyond reconsideration.”

Windows 11 finally added the ability to put the taskbar on any edge of the screen, but only from Settings. Many, including me, suggested bringing back Windows 10’s “Lock the taskbar” to stop accidental drags, but Baca’s answer explains why Microsoft doesn’t think it’s that easy.

Microsoft says a lock for the Windows 11 taskbar would create new problems

“For those suggesting an “auto-lock” or lock/unlock setting as a magic solution, it really isn’t that simple,” Baca wrote on X. “You’re introducing additional friction to solve a relatively infrequent task. Now, every time you want to move the taskbar, you first need to unlock it.”

He also explained that “depending on how locking is implemented, you risk interfering with more common interactions, like rearranging icons or moving items in the system tray.”

As you would know, Windows 11 doesn’t have a “Lock the taskbar” option at all, because its taskbar was rebuilt from scratch and didn’t carry over the old code. So, a lock would have to be built anew, and Microsoft would need to decide what it freezes. If it only locks the position, you’re back to having to unlock it again before every move. If it locks more than that, it could get in the way of dragging pinned apps around, which most of us do far more often than moving the taskbar.

According to Baca, the decision came from Windows 10, “where we saw a significant volume of accidental taskbar movements.” Microsoft hasn’t shared any numbers.

In our earlier report, I argued that drag-to-move could return with a lock turned on by default. Fair enough, the trade-off is clearer now.

Microsoft says nobody said “never” about drag-to-move

“First, let’s get the facts straight. No one said “never,”” Baca wrote, adding that Microsoft continuously evaluates “feedback from telemetry, Feedback Hub, social channels, and other sources, weighing it against our design and product priorities.”

“Please don’t turn an explanation of a design decision into a declaration that something will “NEVER” happen. That’s simply not what I said,” he added.

Baca’s May Windows Insider blog post said Microsoft is “evaluating additional features like different taskbar positions per monitor and drag and drop,” and Microsoft also had been testing a right-click menu with Left, Top, Right, and Bottom buttons when they first announced the movable taskbar, and we found that the leftover code still exists, which, in my opinion, is a better idea if dragging the taskbar is off the table.

History is on his side too. In 2022, Microsoft said the movable taskbar wasn’t returning anytime soon, and it came back in 2026. In 2021, Microsoft said “dragging a file onto an app in the taskbar to open it in that app is not supported in Windows 11,” and that returned with the Windows 11 2022 Update. Never combine taskbar buttons also made a comeback.

To be clear, Microsoft hasn’t promised drag-to-move or given any timeline.

Windows 11’s taskbar serves over a billion people, and every change has trade-offs

“Windows is a complex system used by over a billion people in countless different ways,” says Baca. “Every decision introduces tradeoffs, dependencies, and permutations that we need to consider.”

In another reply, he listed “User research, implementation details, technical constraints, accessibility, consistency” among the factors, and said, “Not everyone has visibility into the full picture.” He also pushed back on calling the setting hidden, saying a single right-click “is hardly buried.”

Baca even said he’s “100% supportive of third-party software that extends Windows,” and for people who move their taskbar often and aren’t worried about accidental drags, third-party drag tools are “perfect.”

Credit where it’s due, it’s rare to see a Microsoft VP explain a design decision in this much detail, in public, and then admit, “That doesn’t mean every decision we make is perfect or beyond criticism. Far from it!” Anyway, I like that Microsoft is being more transparent about their decisions.

“There’s always room for improvement, and we are always listening, learning, and acting on feedback,” says Baca. Drag-to-move isn’t on the way, but the door is still open.

Would you use an unlock step if it meant getting drag-to-move back? Let us know in the comments.

title: Linux App Release Roundup (October 2026)
author: OMG! Ubuntu!
content:
October’s Linux app releases brought plenty of treats, a couple of tricks and mercifully few frights. In this post, I recap the updates that landed last month.

There were other spooks in the shadows with a spotlight. October gave us a double-whammy of Firefox and Calibre updates, with JEPG XL support added in the former and AI reading voices in the latter – among other changes in both.

It also delivered a ‘fully rebuilt’ ONLYOFFICE 10.0 with optional AI tools and KeePassXC 2.8, which added its long-awaited support for Wayland auto-type. System cleaning tool BleachBit fixed issues with admin cleaning on Linux.

With October 2026 now six feet under, here’s what else crept on to the desktop.

OpenShot 4.1 added native text typing

The OpenShot video editor been on a roll of late, adding scores of long-requested features like colour grading and screen capture.

OpenShot 4.1 continues the trend, debuting a new on-canvas text tool, making it easier to create lower thirds, captions and credits, without needing to use SVG or Blender titles, or open the Title editor for each.

The text Edit Style dialog was also redesigned to make it easier to customise the look of on-screen text elements, and copy styles between different text elements.

And the video editor’s pre-existing auto-optimise feature, which creates smaller, optimised copies of video footage for editing but exports full quality versions, now detects more clips suitable for optimising.

With this video editor now coded by LLMs, it’s no surprise to see its own support for AI-related workflows expand too. v4.1 adds CLI automation for export and basic edits so that users can ‘prompt’ agents tools like Claude Code to undertake tasks.

Beyond that, an updated export dialog, more keyboard shortcuts, keyframe and timeline tweaks and general performance improvements on the timeline, preview files, and so on.

OpenShot 4.1 is available to download from the OpenShot website, the Snap Store, Flathub or a PPA – the OpenShot PPA now has builds for Arm64.

FBReader 2.5 unveiled a new library

Cross-platform ebook reader FBReader issued a release candidate of its upcoming 2.5 release for Windows, macOS and Linux (and a second as I was compiling this post).

Biggest change is the redesigned library view, which now supports favourites, custom shelves and batch actions. There’s also integration with the Readino bookshop, enabled by default in the UK, US and Australia, to browse and buy books from within the app.

Another new integration is Screvi, a “service for collecting and organising book highlights and notes from different reading platforms, including Kindle and Kobo”.

On the desktop, FBReader 2.5 can read books aloud using the system text-to-speech engine. It can also play audio and video content inside of EPUB files and open CBR and CB7 comic archives. OPDS 2.0 catalogue support was added too.

A stable 2.5 release is due in the coming weeks.

Download the latest Linux release candidate from the FBReader website. 

Thunderbird 159 badged its tray icon

Thunderbird 159 was released with a treat for Linux users: unread-mail indicators on the system tray icon, and a message count showing in the tooltip. It’s the little things, right?

Other changes were mainly about exorcising bugs, including issues with missing or truncated attachments, broken message searches, pernickety printing behaviour and sync issues with CalDAV and CardDAV.

Other buffs bolster performance and reliability, like taming excessive Microsoft Graph requests, reducing CPU usage from malformed message databases and smoothing out startup hangs when restoring open tabs.

Download the latest from the Thunderbird website.

OBS Studio 33.0 reworked its plugins

OBS Studio 33.0 slipped out, a sizeable update to the popular streaming and screencasting software that changes where plugins are installed, with built-in and third-party plugins now put in separate locations. Existing installs with plugins aren’t affected until v34.0.

The preview window has improved source snapping, with visual indicators to show where each sources’ edges are and letting them snap to the corresponding edge of another. And hidden sources are no longer selecting or triggered when positioning visible ones.

Under the hood, OBS v33 updates its embedded Chromium framework from version 127 to 150 and adds NVENC hardware encoding support for ARM laptops with NVIDIA GPUs.

OBS 33.0 drops support for Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, so if you currently get updates via the OBS Studio PPA, be aware that you won’t get this update from it. You may want to switch to the unofficial snap package instead.

Get OBS Studio from the official website for supported platforms.

Haruna 1.9 made OSD configurable

Haruna 1.9.0 came out in October. The streamlined, Qt6 media player gained menu options and shortcuts for open folders, a new OSD settings panel to control over what options appear on screen and a transcript panel for viewing all subtitles.

Chapter markers were also simplified. They now show as a vertical line in the seek bar, with chapter titles viewable via a tooltip (along with time position and frame thumbnail).

Other additions include an option to disable explanatory tooltips, a new database settings page and a variety of playlist tweaks. When streaming a video from YouTube via the player, the seekbar shows the buffered section, which you can click in to skip ahead.

Haruna is available for install from Flathub.

Tributary 0.7.2 began mastering

Music player Tributary continues to round-out its tribute to Rhythmbox, with October providing two alpha updates.

The 0.7.1 alpha restored a ‘missing’ EQ button in the header bar, which would vanish depending on state and desktop, and the track list now fills the window all the way to the right edge, no including after resizing.

The v0.7.2 alpha released brought a faster way to jump back to the playing track: a quick press of ctrl + j. It also restored a missing equaliser icon, improved its visibility with dark themes and updated network and hashing libraries to improve its security.

While still far from perfect, it’s shaping up well.

Download the latest alpha from the Tributary GitHub releases page.

Scribus 1.7.4 tabled more changes

Open-source desktop publishing software Scribus put out a new development build, v1.7.4, with an overhaul for table editing. Tables now have spreadsheet-style selection and keyboard navigation, conditional formatting and support for pasting from other applications. 

The update also improved right-to-left and bidirectional text support, added a first-run setup wizard and introduced user-editing page-size templates

Other changes include improved right-to-left and bidirectional text support and a new first-run setup wizard to improve setup. Users who work with linked text frames can now select an entire text chain with a single menu action.

Beyond that, seven memory-safety vulnerabilities in image loaders and import filters are also fixed and those same security patches are included in the stable Scribus 1.6.7 release, which also arrived alongside the 1.7.4 development one.

Download Scribus development builds from the project Sourceforge.

Blanc web browser filled in the blanks

Blanc, the Electron-based and AI-sired web browser Blanc, put out more than 20 updates since I took a look at it in September. The amount of changes is large, so I can’t run though it all, but a few choice highlights include:

  • Customizable mouse gestures
  • Time-of-day wallpaper for the start page
  • Linux AppImage no longer requires FUSE2
  • uBlock Origin integrated
  • About & Trust section in settings
  • Browser localisations now including German, Italian and Portuguese
  • Kagi search engine support, including live suggestions, and !bangs
  • Expanded tab customisation, renaming and colour options
  • Various changes to the island UX and island behaviours

Plus, a fair bit more besides.

Check out the official website for more details and download links.

Smaller updates of note

Kdenlive issued the second maintenance release of the 26.08 series with bug fixes and stability improvements, including better project handling and ability to set the frame count to start at 1 in the Dynamic Text filter.

qBittorrent 5.3.0 landed, moving its default build to the libtorrent 2.2 series. While the shift should reduce I/O issues for those coming from the 1.2 series, it may cause issues for heavy seeders as it’s has worse read performance.

And Cine, the GTK4/libadwaita video player, delivered 1.8.8 update that boosted its startup performance, fixed mouse click actions not always working and made its initial window size more condition on the screen size its shown on.

That’s it’s for this roundup. As ever, if you learn of a software update that you think other readers of this site may be interested in knowing about, get in touch via the contact form – your news tips, typo pokes and article suggestions are much appreciated.

title: Microsoft doesn’t care if you hate OneDrive, kills Windows 11’s best local way to...
author: Abhijith M B
summary: Microsoft confirmed "PC-to-PC Migration is no longer available" just a year after launching it. We compare what the local Wi-Fi transfer tool moved (any folder, 118GB in Microsoft's own demo) with Win...
content:
Windows 11’s PC-to-PC Migration, which moved your files and settings from an old PC to a new one over your local network, is no longer available. Microsoft removed it with the September Optional update, and the change reached everyone with the October 13 Patch Tuesday update (KB5127648). Microsoft now wants you to use Windows Backup, which syncs your folders to OneDrive and restores them through your Microsoft account.

If you’re moving more than OneDrive’s free 5GB, or you don’t want your personal files in the cloud, Windows no longer has a guided way to help. Ironically, Microsoft’s screenshots of the now-deprecated PC-to-PC Migration tool show it moving 118GB of files in one go.

Microsoft confirms Windows 11’s PC-to-PC Migration is gone, nudges users to Windows Backup

In the KB5124010 release notes, Microsoft says, “PC-to-PC Migration is no longer available. This feature, introduced through a phased rollout, previously allowed you to transfer files and settings directly from your previous PC when setting up a new Windows PC.”

The company’s recommendation is pretty obvious. “To back up and restore your files, settings, and other supported items when moving to a new PC, use Windows Backup.” Since the October 2026 Patch Tuesday update (KB5127648) includes the September preview changes, the tool is gone from regular Windows 11 PCs as well, though Microsoft lists this as a gradual rollout.

We spotted the removal in September, and the PC-to-PC transfer support page now rather frigidly says, “This feature is no longer available. Use Windows Backup and Restore instead.”

Microsoft hasn’t said why they pulled an impressive and useful feature. But with the local option gone, the only guided way to move to a new Windows 11 PC now goes through OneDrive. You can still copy files with a USB drive, an external disk, or a network share, but you’re on your own there.

Windows Backup and OneDrive can’t replace a local PC-to-PC transfer

PC-to-PC Migration ran during the new PC’s setup. You paired both PCs with the old PC’s name and a one-time code, picked your folders, and let the transfer run over Wi-Fi or Ethernet. The old PC could run Windows 10 or Windows 11, while the new one needed Windows 11, version 2024 or later.

It wasn’t perfect. According to Microsoft, it skipped installed apps, saved passwords and sign-in credentials, OneDrive files, BitLocker-encrypted drives and system folders like Program Files. But it could move files “saved across folders or drives,” including Downloads and custom folders outside your user profile. That said, the software giant could’ve continued development to make this work better.

Windows Backup needs a personal Microsoft account (work and school accounts are out), and the folders it backs up, Desktop, Documents, Pictures, Videos and Music, sync to OneDrive. A free account gets 5GB of storage, and anything beyond that means you’ll have to pay for more, which is quite unreasonable when the company killed their only alternative that worked for free.

Credit where it’s due, Windows Backup remembers things the local tool didn’t, like your installed apps, Wi-Fi networks, and passwords, and you can restore all of it on any PC. Note that apps still need to be reinstalled from their pins.

Here’s how PC-to-PC Migration and Windows Backup compare:

PC-to-PC Migration Windows Backup
Transfer method Local Wi-Fi or Ethernet OneDrive cloud sync
Storage limit Space on the new PC 5GB free on OneDrive
Folders Any folder or drive Five user folders
Apps Not transferred App list, reinstall needed
Passwords and Wi-Fi Not transferred Backed up
Status Removed Available

 

Here’s a funny analogy: one feature is a backup service, and the other was a moving truck. But Microsoft just told you to rent storage!

Microsoft brought back Windows 7’s Easy Transfer, then killed it in a year

If you remember Windows Easy Transfer from the Windows 7 days, this was its spiritual successor. We first spotted Windows 11 testing it in May 2025, and Microsoft confirmed the rollout in its June 2025 Insider blog, saying, “We are releasing in phases for a smooth experience and will provide more details soon.”

By July, Microsoft had a full support document explaining how it works. Just over a year later, the feature was gone, first from Release Preview builds on September 10, then from the optional update and October’s Patch Tuesday.

What boggles me is that Microsoft spent a lot of engineering resources building and documenting a fix for one of the oldest annoyances of setting up a new Windows PC, then dropped it without a word.

Windows Backup is handy if you already use OneDrive. But Microsoft didn’t have to kill the local option to make OneDrive useful. How do you plan to move to your next Windows PC?

title: New VOLTA Infostealer Uses Claude, Gemini, and Kimi AI to Rank Victims by Financial Value
author: The Hacker News
summary: Cybersecurity researchers have discovered a new Windows infostealer malware called VOLTA-AUTODOXER  (aka VOLTA) that makes use of a large language model (LLM) to rank a victim's stolen data by their monetization value. content:
Cybersecurity researchers have discovered a new Windows infostealer malware called VOLTA-AUTODOXER (aka VOLTA) that makes use of a large language model (LLM) to rank a victim's stolen data by their monetization value.

Like other typical stealer families, VOLTA is equipped to harvest passwords and cookies from Chromium-based web browsers; data from Outlook profiles and Slack workspaces; payment cards; cryptocurrency wallet seed phrases; Discord, Telegram, Steam, and Roblox sessions; Microsoft OAuth tokens; SSH and cloud-provider keys; Wi-Fi profiles; and screenshots.

"VOLTA builds a structured evidence bundle about the person behind the machine," Cisco Talos researcher Ryan Fetterman said. "This bundle contains geolocation and home address, employer and employer domain, inferred birth year, card last-4 digits, Slack workspaces, document authorship metadata, iPhone backup indicators, and a live Roblox account valuation."

To make this information more valuable, the malware uses stolen session access to search the victim's Gmail account for receipts to corroborate the home address by extracting emails related to Amazon, DoorDash, Uber Eats, Grubhub, Walmart, and PayPal.

Once the necessary information is collected, the bundle is serialized and fed into an artificial intelligence (AI) system for analysis using OpenRouter, a unified LLM API gateway and routing service, along with a system prompt. The requests are defaulted to Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.6, failing which it falls back to Moonshot AI's Kimi K2 and Google's Gemini 2.5 Flash.

"VOLTA uses a multi-model architecture to fall back resiliently if it hits a model's refusal, checking each response for phrases like 'I can't' or 'I'm not able,' before passing on to a chain of up to three models," Talos said.

VOLTA features a 240-word system prompt that instructs the model to assume the role of a "forensic intelligence analyst" responsible for drafting a target assessment based on data from a structured evidence bundle. "The bundle is the ONLY permissible source of facts; your training knowledge must never supply a fact about the subject," reads a line from the prompt.

"The required output includes a section titled 'WHAT THEY'RE WORTH' with valuables ranked by monetization with a low/medium/high tier, and a section on 'THEIR OPSEC' containing an assessment of the victim's security posture and password hygiene," Talos explained.

"The model is the operator's triage analyst; it turns a raw credential log into a prioritized and citation-backed dossier of the victim and their monetizable assets."

Data exfiltration happens over Telegram at three different stages -

  • Right after the stealer runs, containing details about browser passwords, cookies, payment cards, cryptocurrency wallets; Discord, Steam, and Roblox tokens; Wi-Fi passwords, and screenshots
  • After the AI call, which includes the captured data and the results of the LLM analysis
  • After the live enrichment step, which includes Gmail receipts and order histories

What's more, VOLTA makes use of a template containing six slots that are filled in at build time. This includes the  Telegram channel used for data exfiltration, API keys, and other settings.

This approach suggests that the malware author is likely either advertising a builder kit to prospective customers or operating it as a bespoke tool under their control to compile a custom binary for each order.

"If VOLTA is indeed a commoditized malware, then the AI dossier capability isn't something the author invented for their own operations," Talos said. "It is a feature which enables a customer of any level of sophistication to point it at victims and start receiving ranked target assessments in their Telegram inbox."

"VOLTA is a mature stealer with a late-stage AI layer added for one purpose: relieving the operator of analytical work. The axis of AI improvement here is not speed or scale but effort displacement."

The disclosure comes as adversarial adoption of generative AI (aka GenAI) is quickly becoming the new normal, as threat actors incorporate the technology into their workflows to develop custom tools or find valuable data, thereby increasing the likelihood of success of their attacks.

"GenAI technologies are also well suited to examine massive amounts of data for the purposes of classification or content searching," Zscaler ThreatLabz said. "Once an attacker has access to the victim’s system, GenAI can therefore be used to search all materials to which a victim's system has access, seeking the most valuable or sensitive data for theft or encryption during the next phase of the attack."

A ransomware actor can leverage this method to identify and acquire the most sensitive data from a compromised network, maximizing the chances that the victim will pay up.

Last week, Talos also detailed an AI-enabled framework called NIK C2 that gives attackers remote access, credential theft, keylogging, defense evasion, surveillance, and ransomware capabilities, while integrating an OpenAI client to send stolen data for AI analysis within the compromised session.

A Go-based, Windows remote access tool, NIK C2 grants persistent control over compromised hosts and supports over 52 commands sent by a command-and-control (C2) server to collect a wide range of data.

The OpenAI integration is notable for the fact that the threat actor can abuse a victim's own OpenAI API key to execute the AI-driven analysis. Specifically, the plant checks if the actor has supplied an API key. In the absence of one, it scans the victim's environment variables for the string "OPENAI_API_KEY" and uses it.

This is a form of LLMjacking, where bad actors steal access to another party's AI model to run their own operations – in this case, against the victim itself – while the legitimate owner pays for the computing power. In addition, it allows the attacker to evade detection by obscuring who made the requests.

"This fallback is not a backup mechanism for API key resolution. It is a deliberate design with significant operational implications," Talos said. "If the victim has configured an OpenAI account on their machine, that account's API key will be used to fund the actor's AI inference."

"NIK C2 reshapes adversary tradecraft by collapsing collection and exploitation into a single continuous session, effectively erasing the offline processing delays that historically granted defenders critical detection windows," Talos said.
